margin-left: -0.04398em; margin-right: 0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mathnormal mtight">s</span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.15em;"><span class=""></span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.277778em;"></span><span class="mrel">=</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.277778em;"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.58056em; vertical-align: -0.15em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.04398em;">z</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.280556em;"><span class="" style="top: -2.55em; margin-left: -0.04398em; margin-right: 0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mathnormal mtight">t</span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.15em;"><span class=""></span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.277778em;"></span><span class="mrel">=</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.277778em;"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 1em; vertical-align: -0.25em;"></span><span class="mopen">(</span><span class="mord">1</span><span class="mpunct">,</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.166667em;"></span><span class="mord">0</span><span class="mpunct">,</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.166667em;"></span><span class="minner">…</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.166667em;"></span><span class="mpunct">,</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.166667em;"></span><span class="mord">0</span><span class="mclose">)</span><span class="mord">.</span></span></span></span></span></span></p>
<p>for every input.</p>
<p>This perfectly satisfies</p>
<p><span class="katex--display"><span class="katex-display"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="block"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><mo>≈</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo separator="true">,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex"> z_s \approx z_t, </annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.63312em; vertical-align: -0.15em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.04398em;">z</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.151392em;"><span class="" style="top: -2.55em; margin-left: -0.04398em; margin-right: 0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mathnormal mtight">s</span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.15em;"><span class=""></span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.277778em;"></span><span class="mrel">≈</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.277778em;"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.625em; vertical-align: -0.19444em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.04398em;">z</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.280556em;"><span class="" style="top: -2.55em; margin-left: -0.04398em; margin-right: 0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mathnormal mtight">t</span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.15em;"><span class=""></span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mpunct">,</span></span></span></span></span></span></p>
<p>but every input now has exactly the same representation.</p>
<p>That is complete collapse.</p>
<p>With stop-gradient, the teacher cannot immediately move toward whatever solution the student finds because it receives no gradients.</p>
<p>Instead, the teacher changes only gradually through EMA.</p>
<p>The student therefore has to match a slowly evolving target instead of one that instantly follows it.</p>
<p>This greatly reduces the tendency for both networks to converge to the same constant representation.</p>
<hr>
<h3 id="limitation-2">Limitation</h3>
<p>Unlike contrastive learning or clustering-based methods, there is <strong>no complete mathematical proof</strong> explaining exactly why this training procedure consistently avoids collapse.</p>
<p>The combination of</p>
<ul>
<li>stop-gradient,</li>
<li>EMA teacher updates,</li>
<li>predictor networks (used in methods like BYOL),</li>
</ul>
<p>works well empirically, but there is no universally accepted theory describing the exact objective or distribution being optimized, or proving under what conditions collapse is impossible.</p>
<p>As a result, performance depends heavily on implementation details and hyperparameters such as the EMA coefficient <span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>m</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.43056em; vertical-align: 0em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal">m</span></span></span></span></span>, learning rate, optimizer, and predictor design. This makes the method harder to analyze theoretically and more difficult to adapt reliably to new domains.</p>
<p>By relying on implicit architectural constraints, the field became bottlenecked by engineering complexity. To advance toward mathematically optimal JEPAs, the first necessary step was eliminating these asymmetric heuristics entirely.</p>
<h2 id="are-you-ready-for-part-4-where-we-explore-the-modularity-objective-and-how-returning-to-a-symmetric-architecture-unlocks-independent-multi-modal-branch-regularization">Are you ready for Part 4, where we explore the Modularity Objective and how returning to a symmetric architecture unlocks independent, multi-modal branch regularization?</h2>
<h2 id="the-limitation-of-architectural-heuristics">The Limitation of Architectural Heuristics</h2>
<p>Although the methods discussed above successfully reduce or prevent collapse, they all rely on carefully designed architectural mechanisms rather than an explicit mathematical guarantee.</p>
<p>Contrastive methods require negative samples.</p>
<p>Clustering methods require balanced prototype assignments.</p>
<p>Asymmetric methods require components such as EMA teachers, stop-gradient, or predictor networks.</p>
<p>These mechanisms certainly work in practice, but they raise a deeper question:</p>
<blockquote>
<p><strong>Should preventing collapse really depend on the architecture?</strong></p>
</blockquote>
<p>Ideally, the answer should be <strong>no</strong>.</p>
<p>The role of the architecture is to compute representations,</p>
<p><span class="katex--display"><span class="katex-display"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="block"><semantics><mrow><mi>z</mi><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>f</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo separator="true">,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">
z=f_\theta(x),
</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.43056em; vertical-align: 0em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.04398em;">z</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.277778em;"></span><span class="mrel">=</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.277778em;"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 1em; vertical-align: -0.25em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.10764em;">f</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.336108em;"><span class="" style="top: -2.55em; margin-left: -0.10764em; margin-right: 0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mathnormal mtight" style="margin-right: 0.02778em;">θ</span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.15em;"><span class=""></span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mopen">(</span><span class="mord mathnormal">x</span><span class="mclose">)</span><span class="mpunct">,</span></span></span></span></span></span></p>
<p>while the role of the objective function is to define what makes those representations good.</p>
<p>If changing architectural details—such as removing a predictor network or stop-gradient—causes training to collapse, then part of the optimization problem is being solved implicitly by the architecture rather than explicitly by the loss function.</p>
<p>This has two important consequences.</p>
<p>First, the learning process becomes difficult to analyze theoretically because the optimization behavior depends on implementation details instead of a clearly defined objective.</p>
<p>Second, architectural constraints reduce flexibility. Methods that depend on shared weights, predictor networks, or teacher-student asymmetry become harder to extend to heterogeneous architectures or different data modalities.</p>
<p>These limitations motivate a more fundamental question:</p>
<blockquote>
<p><strong>Can collapse be prevented directly through the objective function, without relying on architectural tricks?</strong></p>
</blockquote>
<p>Answering this question leads to the principle of <strong>modularity</strong>, where the responsibility for learning meaningful representations is transferred from the architecture to the loss function itself.</p>
<h3 id="part-4-the-modularity-objective">Part 4: The Modularity Objective</h3>
<p><strong>Breaking the Symmetry Dependence</strong> The heuristics detailed in Part 3—such as stop-gradients, predictor networks, and exponential moving average (EMA) teachers—force a strict structural dependency between the two branches of a Joint-Embedding Architecture. To mathematically guarantee collapse prevention without these crutches, the framework must decouple <em>how the branches are compared</em> from <em>how they are regularized</em>.</p>
<p><strong>Independent Branch Regularization</strong> The modularity objective posits that topological collapse can be eradicated by explicitly enforcing statistical properties on the batch of embeddings within each branch independently.</p>
<p>Let <span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>Z</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Z</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.68333em; margin-right: 0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight"><span class="mord mtight">′</span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span> be the batches of embeddings produced by two distinct encoders, <span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>f</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f_\theta</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.88888em; margin-left: -0.10764em; margin-right: 0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight"><span class="mord mtight"><span class="mord mathnormal mtight" style="margin-right: 0.02778em;">θ</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.682829em;"><span class="" style="top: -2.786em; margin-right: 0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight"><span class="mord mtight">′</span></span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.283108em;"><span class=""></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span>. Instead of using cross-branch statistical dependencies (like the cross-correlation matrix in Barlow Twins) to stabilize training, the global loss is decomposed into an invariance term <span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>s</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.43056em; <p><strong>Unlocking Multi-Modal Freedom</strong></p>
<p>This explicit mathematical modularity yields profound architectural freedom:</p>
<ul>
<li>
<p><strong>No Shared Weights or Architectures:</strong> The encoders <span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>f</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f_\theta</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.88888em; vertical-align: -0.19444em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.10764em;">f</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.336108em;"><span class="" style="top: -2.55em; margin-left: -0.10764em; margin-right: 0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mathnormal mtight" style="margin-right: 0.02778em;">θ</span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.15em;"><span class=""></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span> and <span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>f</mi><msup><mi>θ</mi><mo mathvariant="normal" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">′</mo></msup><mo mathvariant="normal" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">′</mo></msubsup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f'_{\theta'}</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 1.035em; vertical-align: -0.283108em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.10764em;">f</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.751892em;"><span class="" style="top: -2.41689em; margin-left: -0.10764em; margin-right: 0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight"><span class="mord mtight"><span class="mord mathnormal mtight" style="margin-right: 0.02778em;">θ</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.682829em;"><span class="" style="top: -2.786em; They do not need to share parameters or even have the same network topology.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><strong>Asymmetric Modalities:</strong> Cross-branch regularizers assume the outputs from both branches exhibit similar statistics. By regularizing independently, one branch can encode discrete text sequences while the other encodes continuous image pixels. The independent regularization naturally handles the distinct statistics of each modality without causing numerical instability.</p>
</li>
</ul>
<p>This modular, heuristic-free paradigm forms the exact mathematical foundation for Variance-Invariance-Covariance Regularization (VICReg). We will mathematically deconstruct the exact mechanics of these <span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>v</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.43056em; vertical-align: 0em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.03588em;">v</span></span></span></span></span> and <span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>c</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.43056em; vertical-align: 0em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal">c</span></span></span></span></span> terms as we transition into Module 2.</p>
<h1 id="part-4-the-modularity-objective-1">Part 4: The Modularity Objective</h1>
<h2 id="separating-two-independent-problems">Separating Two Independent Problems</h2>
<p>Up to this point, every anti-collapse method has attempted to solve two fundamentally different problems using one tightly coupled mechanism.</p>
<p>Given two embedding batches,</p>
<p><span class="katex--display"><span class="katex-display"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="block"><semantics><mrow><mi>Z</mi><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>f</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo separator="true">,</mo><mspace width="2em"></mspace><msup><mi>Z</mi><mo mathvariant="normal" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">′</mo></msup><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>f</mi><msup><mi>θ</mi><mo mathvariant="normal" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">′</mo></msup></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mo mathvariant="normal" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">′</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo separator="true">,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">
Z=f_\theta(x), \qquad
Z'=f_{\theta'}(x'),
</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.68333em; vertical-align: 0em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.07153em;">Z</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.277778em;"></span><span class="mrel">=</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.277778em;"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 1.05189em; <p>the architecture must simultaneously satisfy two completely different objectives.</p>
<h3 id="objective-1-prediction-consistency">Objective 1: Prediction Consistency</h3>
<p>The first requirement is that both views of the same sample produce similar representations.</p>
<p>Mathematically,</p>
<p><span class="katex--display"><span class="katex-display"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="block"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>≈</mo><msubsup><mi>z</mi><mi>i</mi><mo mathvariant="normal" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">′</mo></msubsup><mi mathvariant="normal">.</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">
z_i \approx z_i'.
</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.63312em; vertical-align: -0.15em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.04398em;">z</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.311664em;"><span class="" style="top: -2.55em; margin-left: -0.04398em; margin-right: 0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mathnormal mtight">i</span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.15em;"><span class=""></span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.277778em;"></span><span class="mrel">≈</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.277778em;"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 1.04889em; vertical-align: -0.247em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.04398em;">z</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.801892em;"><span class="" style="top: -2.453em; margin-left: -0.04398em; margin-right: 0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mathnormal mtight">i</span></span></span><span class="" style="top: -3.113em; margin-right: 0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight"><span class="mord mtight">′</span></span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.247em;"><span class=""></span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mord">.</span></span></span></span></span></span></p>
<p>This is purely a relationship <strong>between the two branches</strong>.</p>
<p>It says nothing about whether either representation is actually informative.</p>
<p>For example,</p>
<p><span class="katex--display"><span class="katex-display"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="block"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><msubsup><mi>z</mi><mi>i</mi><mo mathvariant="normal" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">′</mo></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo separator="true">,</mo><mn>0</mn><mo separator="true">,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo separator="true">,</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo separator="true">,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">
z_i=z_i'=(0,0,\ldots,0),
</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.58056em; vertical-align: -0.15em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.04398em;">z</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.311664em;"><span class="" style="top: -2.55em; margin-left: -0.04398em; margin-right: 0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mathnormal mtight">i</span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.15em;"><span class=""></span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.277778em;"></span><span class="mrel">=</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.277778em;"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 1.04889em; vertical-align: -0.247em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.04398em;">z</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.801892em;"><span class="" style="top: -2.453em; margin-left: -0.04398em; margin-right: 0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mathnormal mtight">i</span></span></span><span class="" style="top: -3.113em; margin-right: 0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight"><span class="mord mtight">′</span></span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.247em;"><span class=""></span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.277778em;"></span><span class="mrel">=</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.277778em;"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 1em; vertical-align: -0.25em;"></span><span class="mopen">(</span><span class="mord">0</span><span class="mpunct">,</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.166667em;"></span><span class="mord">0</span><span class="mpunct">,</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.166667em;"></span><span class="minner">…</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.166667em;"></span><span class="mpunct">,</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.166667em;"></span><span class="mord">0</span><span class="mclose">)</span><span class="mpunct">,</span></span></span></span></span></span></p>
<p>perfectly satisfies this requirement, even though every representation has completely collapsed.</p>
<p>Therefore, matching the two branches alone cannot prevent collapse.</p>
<hr>
<h3 id="objective-2-representation-quality">Objective 2: Representation Quality</h3>
<p>Each encoder must also produce embeddings that preserve information about the input.</p>
<p>This requirement concerns only one branch at a time.</p>
<p>If encoder <span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>f</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f_\theta</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.88888em; vertical-align: -0.19444em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.10764em;">f</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.336108em;"><span class="" style="top: -2.55em; margin-left: -0.10764em; margin-right: 0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mathnormal mtight" style="margin-right: 0.02778em;">θ</span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.15em;"><span class=""></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span> collapses,</p>
<p><span class="katex--display"><span class="katex-display"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="block"><semantics><mrow><mi>Z</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo fence="true">[</mo><mtable rowspacing="0.1600em" columnalign="center" columnspacing="1em"><mtr><mtd><mstyle scriptlevel="0" displaystyle="false"><mi>c</mi></mstyle></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd><mstyle scriptlevel="0" displaystyle="false"><mi>c</mi></mstyle></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd><mstyle scriptlevel="0" displaystyle="false"><mi><mi mathvariant="normal">⋮</mi><mpadded height="+0em" voffset="0em"><mspace mathbackground="black" width="0em" height="1.5em"></mspace></mpadded></mi></mstyle></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd><mstyle scriptlevel="0" displaystyle="false"><mi>c</mi></mstyle></mtd></mtr></mtable><mo fence="true">]</mo></mrow><mo separator="true">,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">
Z=
\begin{bmatrix}
c\\
c\\
\vdots\\
c
\end{bmatrix},
</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.68333em; vertical-align: 0em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.07153em;">Z</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.277778em;"></span><span class="mrel">=</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.277778em;"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 5.46em; vertical-align: -2.48em;"></span><span class="minner"><span class="mopen"><span class="delimsizing mult"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 2.95003em;"><span class="" style="top: -2.01101em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 3.81603em;"></span><span class="delimsizinginner delim-size4"><span class="">⎣</span></span></span><span class="" style="top: -3.15801em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 3.81603em;"></span><span class="" style="height: 1.81603em; width: 0.667em;"><svg width="0.667em" height="1.8160299999999996em" style="width:0.667em" viewBox="0 0 667 1816" preserveAspectRatio="xMinYMin"><path d="M319 0 H403 V1816 H319z M319 0 H403 V1816 H319z"></path></svg></span></span><span class="" style="top: -5.61106em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 3.81603em;"></span><span class="delimsizinginner delim-size4"><span class="">⎡</span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 2.45003em;"><span class=""></span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mord"><span class="mtable"><span class="col-align-c"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 2.98em;"><span class="" style="top: -5.8275em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 3.6875em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal">c</span></span></span><span class="" style="top: -4.6275em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 3.6875em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal">c</span></span></span><span class="" style="top: -2.7675em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 3.6875em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord"><span class="mord">⋮</span><span class="mord rule" style="border-right-width: 0em; border-top-width: 1.5em; bottom: 0em;"></span></span></span></span><span class="" style="top: -1.5675em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 3.6875em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal">c</span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 2.48em;"><span class=""></span></span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mclose"><span class="delimsizing mult"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 2.95003em;"><span class="" style="top: -2.01101em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 3.81603em;"></span><span class="delimsizinginner delim-size4"><span class="">⎦</span></span></span><span class="" style="top: -3.15801em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 3.81603em;"></span><span class="" style="height: 1.81603em; width: 0.667em;"><svg width="0.667em" height="1.8160299999999996em" style="width:0.667em" viewBox="0 0 667 1816" preserveAspectRatio="xMinYMin"><path d="M263 0 H347 V1816 H263z M263 0 H347 V1816 H263z"></path></svg></span></span><span class="" style="top: -5.61106em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 3.81603em;"></span><span class="delimsizinginner delim-size4"><span class="">⎤</span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 2.45003em;"><span class=""></span></span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.166667em;"></span><span class="mpunct">,</span></span></span></span></span></span></p>
<p>then all information about the inputs has been destroyed regardless of what the second encoder produces.</p>
<p>Likewise, if <span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>f</mi><msup><mi>θ</mi><mo mathvariant="normal" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">′</mo></msup></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f_{\theta'}</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.88888em; vertical-align: -0.19444em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.10764em;">f</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.336108em;"><span class="" style="top: -2.55em; margin-left: -0.10764em; margin-right: 0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight"><span class="mord mtight"><span class="mord mathnormal mtight" style="margin-right: 0.02778em;">θ</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.682829em;"><span class="" style="top: -2.786em; margin-right: 0.0714286em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 2.5em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size3 size1 mtight"><span class="mord mtight"><span class="mord mtight">′</span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.15em;"><span class=""></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span> collapses, the same problem occurs independently.</p>
<p>Whether one encoder collapses depends entirely on the statistical structure of its own embedding space—not on the other encoder.</p>
<p>This is an entirely separate mathematical problem from prediction consistency.</p>
<hr>
<h2 id="the-problem-with-previous-methods">The Problem with Previous Methods</h2>
<p>The heuristic methods from Part 3 do not separate these two objectives.</p>
<p>Instead, they mix them together through architectural constraints.</p>
<p>Examples include</p>
<ul>
<li>Negative samples</li>
<li>Prototype assignments</li>
<li>Stop-gradient</li>
<li>EMA teachers</li>
<li>Predictor networks</li>
</ul>
<p>These mechanisms simultaneously</p>
<ul>
<li>compare the two branches, and</li>
<li>attempt to prevent collapse.</li>
</ul>
<p>As a consequence, collapse prevention becomes dependent on the architecture itself rather than on an explicit mathematical objective.</p>
<p>Removing any of these components often causes the entire training procedure to fail.</p>
<p>The architecture—not the loss function—is doing much of the work.</p>
<hr>
<h2 id="a-first-principles-reformulation">A First-Principles Reformulation</h2>
<p>Instead of asking</p>
<blockquote>
<p><strong>How can one branch stop the other from collapsing?</strong></p>
</blockquote>
<p>we ask a more fundamental question:</p>
<blockquote>
<p><strong>Can each branch be prevented from collapsing entirely on its own?</strong></p>
</blockquote>
<p>If the answer is yes, then collapse prevention no longer requires any interaction between the two branches.</p>
<p>Each encoder can independently guarantee that its embedding space remains informative.</p>
<p>The only remaining interaction between the branches is the prediction objective.</p>
<p>This naturally separates the learning problem into two independent pieces.</p>
<h3 id="cross-branch-objective">Cross-Branch Objective</h3>
<p>The branches should agree on the semantic content of corresponding samples.</p>
<p>Symbolically,</p>
<p><span class="katex--display"><span class="katex-display"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="block"><semantics><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>Z</mi><mo separator="true">,</mo><msup><mi>Z</mi><mo mathvariant="normal" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">′</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">.</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">
s(Z,Z').
</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 1.05189em; vertical-align: -0.25em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal">s</span><span class="mopen">(</span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.07153em;">Z</span><span class="mpunct">,</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.166667em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.07153em;">Z</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.801892em;"><span class="" style="top: -3.113em; margin-right: 0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight"><span class="mord mtight">′</span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mclose">)</span><span class="mord">.</span></span></span></span></span></span></p>
<p>This term compares the two embedding spaces.</p>
<p>Its only purpose is to make matching views produce similar representations.</p>
<hr>
<h3 id="per-branch-regularization">Per-Branch Regularization</h3>
<p>Each embedding space should independently maintain a healthy geometry.</p>
<p>Symbolically,</p>
<p><span class="katex--display"><span class="katex-display"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="block"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>Z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo separator="true">,</mo><mspace width="2em"></mspace><mi>r</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>Z</mi><mo mathvariant="normal" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">′</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">.</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">
r(Z), \qquad r(Z').
</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 1.05189em; vertical-align: -0.25em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.02778em;">r</span><span class="mopen">(</span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.07153em;">Z</span><span class="mclose">)</span><span class="mpunct">,</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 2em;"></span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.166667em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.02778em;">r</span><span class="mopen">(</span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.07153em;">Z</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.801892em;"><span class="" style="top: -3.113em; margin-right: 0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight"><span class="mord mtight">′</span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mclose">)</span><span class="mord">.</span></span></span></span></span></span></p>
<p>These terms never compare one encoder with the other.</p>
<p>They inspect only the statistical properties of a single embedding batch.</p>
<p>If one encoder begins to collapse, its own regularizer produces the corrective gradient.</p>
<p>The other encoder plays no role.</p>
<hr>
<h2 id="the-modular-objective">The Modular Objective</h2>
<p>The global optimization problem therefore decomposes into</p>
<p><span class="katex--display"><span class="katex-display"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="block"><semantics><mtable rowspacing="0.2500em" columnalign="right left" columnspacing="0em"><mtr><mtd><mstyle scriptlevel="0" displaystyle="true"><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>Z</mi><mo separator="true">,</mo><msup><mi>Z</mi><mo mathvariant="normal" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">′</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mstyle></mtd><mtd><mstyle scriptlevel="0" displaystyle="true"><mrow><mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>λ</mi> <mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>Z</mi><mo separator="true">,</mo><msup><mi>Z</mi><mo mathvariant="normal" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">′</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>+</mo><mi>r</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>Z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>+</mo><mi>r</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>Z</mi><mo mathvariant="normal" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">′</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">.</mi></mrow></mstyle></mtd></mtr></mtable><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">
\begin{aligned}
L(Z,Z') &amp;= \lambda\, s(Z,Z') + r(Z) + r(Z').
\end{aligned}
</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 1.5em; vertical-align: -0.5em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mtable"><span class="col-align-r"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 1em;"><span class="" style="top: -3.16em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 3em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal">L</span><span class="mopen">(</span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.07153em;">Z</span><span class="mpunct">,</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.166667em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.07153em;">Z</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.801892em;"><span class="" style="top: -3.113em; margin-right: 0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight"><span class="mord mtight">′</span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mclose">)</span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.5em;"><span class=""></span></span></span></span></span><span class="col-align-l"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 1em;"><span class="" style="top: -3.16em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 3em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord"></span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.277778em;"></span><span class="mrel">=</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.277778em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal">λ</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.166667em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal">s</span><span class="mopen">(</span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.07153em;">Z</span><span class="mpunct">,</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.166667em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.07153em;">Z</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.801892em;"><span class="" style="top: -3.113em; margin-right: 0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight"><span class="mord mtight">′</span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mclose">)</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.222222em;"></span><span class="mbin">+</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.222222em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.02778em;">r</span><span class="mopen">(</span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.07153em;">Z</span><span class="mclose">)</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.222222em;"></span><span class="mbin">+</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.222222em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.02778em;">r</span><span class="mopen">(</span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.07153em;">Z</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.801892em;"><span class="" style="top: -3.113em; margin-right: 0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight"><span class="mord mtight">′</span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mclose">)</span><span class="mord">.</span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.5em;"><span class=""></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></p>
<p>This decomposition has a clear interpretation.</p>
<ul>
<li>
<p><span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>Z</mi><mo separator="true">,</mo><msup><mi>Z</mi><mo mathvariant="normal" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">′</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s(Z,Z')</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 1.00189em; vertical-align: -0.25em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal">s</span><span class="mopen">(</span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.07153em;">Z</span><span class="mpunct">,</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.166667em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.07153em;">Z</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.751892em;"><span class="" style="top: -3.063em; margin-right: 0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight"><span class="mord mtight">′</span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mclose">)</span></span></span></span></span> answers:</p>
<blockquote>
<p><strong>Do corresponding views produce similar embeddings?</strong></p>
</blockquote>
</li>
<li>
<p><span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>Z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r(Z)</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 1em; vertical-align: -0.25em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.02778em;">r</span><span class="mopen">(</span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.07153em;">Z</span><span class="mclose">)</span></span></span></span></span> answers:</p>
<blockquote>
<p><strong>Is the first embedding space still informative?</strong></p>
</blockquote>
</li>
<li>
<p><span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>Z</mi><mo mathvariant="normal" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">′</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r(Z')</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 1.00189em; vertical-align: -0.25em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.02778em;">r</span><span class="mopen">(</span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.07153em;">Z</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.751892em;"><span class="" style="top: -3.063em; margin-right: 0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight"><span class="mord mtight">′</span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mclose">)</span></span></span></span></span> answers:</p>
<blockquote>
<p><strong>Is the second embedding space still informative?</strong></p>
</blockquote>
</li>
</ul>
<p>Each question is solved independently.</p>
<hr>
<h2 id="why-this-matters">Why This Matters</h2>
<p>Because collapse prevention is now entirely local to each encoder,</p>
<ul>
<li>neither branch needs an EMA teacher,</li>
<li>neither branch needs stop-gradient,</li>
<li>neither branch needs predictor asymmetry,</li>
<li>neither branch needs to share parameters,</li>
<li>neither branch even needs the same architecture.</li>
</ul>
<p>The only mathematical connection between the branches is the prediction objective.</p>
<p>Everything responsible for maintaining the quality of an embedding space is handled locally within that embedding space itself.</p>
<p>This principle is called <strong>modularity</strong>.</p>
<p>The remaining question is:</p>
<blockquote>
<p><strong>What specific regularizer <span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo>⋅</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r(\cdot)</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 1em; vertical-align: -0.25em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.02778em;">r</span><span class="mopen">(</span><span class="mord">⋅</span><span class="mclose">)</span></span></span></span></span> guarantees that a single embedding space cannot collapse?</strong></p>
</blockquote>
<p>The next module answers this by decomposing <span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo>⋅</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r(\cdot)</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 1em; vertical-align: -0.25em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.02778em;">r</span><span class="mopen">(</span><span class="mord">⋅</span><span class="mclose">)</span></span></span></span></span> into two explicit statistical constraints: one that prevents complete collapse and one that prevents informational collapse.</p>
<h2 id="why-modularity-changes-the-problem">Why Modularity Changes the Problem</h2>
<p>The significance of modularity is not that it introduces another self-supervised objective.</p>
<p>Its significance is that it changes <strong>how the optimization problem itself is formulated</strong>.</p>
<p>In the heuristic methods discussed previously, collapse prevention is intertwined with the interaction between the two branches.</p>
<p>The optimization depends not only on the objective function but also on architectural mechanisms such as stop-gradient, predictor networks, EMA updates, or balanced prototype assignments.</p>
<p>Consequently, the mathematical objective alone does not completely specify what constitutes a valid solution.</p>
<p>Part of the optimization behavior is hidden inside the architecture.</p>
<p>The modular formulation removes this dependency.</p>
<p>Instead of asking one complicated objective to simultaneously</p>
<ul>
<li>make corresponding views agree,</li>
<li>prevent collapse,</li>
<li>maintain diversity,</li>
<li>and stabilize optimization,</li>
</ul>
<p>these responsibilities are separated into independent mathematical constraints.</p>
<p>The prediction objective answers only one question:</p>
<blockquote>
<p><strong>Do two different views of the same sample produce similar representations?</strong></p>
</blockquote>
<p>The regularization objective answers an entirely different question:</p>
<blockquote>
<p><strong>Is the embedding space itself informative and non-degenerate?</strong></p>
</blockquote>
<p>These questions are logically independent.</p>
<p>Whether two representations agree says nothing about whether they contain useful information.</p>
<p>Likewise, an informative embedding space says nothing about whether two augmented views of the same object will map to similar locations.</p>
<p>Since neither property implies the other, neither objective should be responsible for enforcing both.</p>
<hr>
<h3 id="localizing-collapse-prevention">Localizing Collapse Prevention</h3>
<p>An even deeper consequence follows from this decomposition.</p>
<p>Suppose one encoder begins to collapse.</p>
<p>Its embeddings gradually become</p>
<p><span class="katex--display"><span class="katex-display"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="block"><semantics><mrow><mi>Z</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo fence="true">[</mo><mtable rowspacing="0.1600em" columnalign="center" columnspacing="1em"><mtr><mtd><mstyle scriptlevel="0" displaystyle="false"><mi>c</mi></mstyle></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd><mstyle scriptlevel="0" displaystyle="false"><mi>c</mi></mstyle></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd><mstyle scriptlevel="0" displaystyle="false"><mi><mi mathvariant="normal">⋮</mi><mpadded height="+0em" voffset="0em"><mspace mathbackground="black" width="0em" height="1.5em"></mspace></mpadded></mi></mstyle></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd><mstyle scriptlevel="0" displaystyle="false"><mi>c</mi></mstyle></mtd></mtr></mtable><mo fence="true">]</mo></mrow><mo separator="true">,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">
Z=
\begin{bmatrix}
c\\
c\\
\vdots\\
c
\end{bmatrix},
</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.68333em; vertical-align: 0em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.07153em;">Z</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.277778em;"></span><span class="mrel">=</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.277778em;"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 5.46em; width: 0.667em;"><svg width="0.667em" height="1.8160299999999996em" style="width:0.667em" viewBox="0 0 667 1816" preserveAspectRatio="xMinYMin"><path d="M263 0 H347 V1816 H263z M263 0 H347 V1816 H263z"></path></svg></span></span><span class="" style="top: -5.61106em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 3.81603em;"></span><span class="delimsizinginner delim-size4"><span class="">⎤</span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 2.45003em;"><span class=""></span></span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.166667em;"></span><span class="mpunct">,</span></span></span></span></span></span></p>
<p>where every sample is mapped to the same vector.</p>
<p>Notice where this failure occurs.</p>
<p>It occurs entirely <strong>inside the embedding space produced by that encoder</strong>.</p>
<p>Nothing about the second encoder caused this collapse.</p>
<p>Nothing inside the second encoder can directly repair it.</p>
<p>The problem exists locally.</p>
<p>Therefore, the corrective signal should also be local.</p>
<p>Instead of relying on another branch to detect that collapse has occurred, each encoder should continuously verify that <strong>its own</strong> embedding distribution remains informative.</p>
<p>Mathematically, every encoder becomes responsible for maintaining the quality of its own latent space.</p>
<p>The second encoder is no longer required to “keep the first one honest.”</p>
<p>This is the central idea behind independent branch regularization.</p>
<hr>
<h3 id="architectural-freedom">Architectural Freedom</h3>
<p>Once collapse prevention is local, the interaction between the two branches becomes remarkably simple.</p>
<p>The branches only need to agree on corresponding samples through</p>
<p><span class="katex--display"><span class="katex-display"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="block"><semantics><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>Z</mi><mo separator="true">,</mo><msup><mi>Z</mi><mo mathvariant="normal" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">′</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">.</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">
s(Z,Z').
</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 1.05189em; vertical-align: -0.25em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal">s</span><span class="mopen">(</span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.07153em;">Z</span><span class="mpunct">,</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.166667em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.07153em;">Z</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.801892em;"><span class="" style="top: -3.113em; margin-right: 0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight"><span class="mord mtight">′</span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mclose">)</span><span class="mord">.</span></span></span></span></span></span></p>
<p>Everything else happens independently.</p>
<p>This immediately removes many restrictions that earlier methods required.</p>
<p>The two branches no longer need</p>
<ul>
<li>shared parameters,</li>
<li>identical architectures,</li>
<li>synchronized optimization dynamics,</li>
<li>predictor asymmetry,</li>
<li>exponential moving averages,</li>
<li>or stop-gradient operations.</li>
</ul>
<p>Each encoder can evolve independently while still maintaining a healthy embedding space.</p>
<p>The prediction objective merely aligns the semantic meaning of the two representations.</p>
<p>It is no longer responsible for preventing collapse.</p>
<hr>
<h3 id="separating-the-what-from-the-how">Separating the “What” from the “How”</h3>
<p>This distinction also makes the optimization problem easier to understand mathematically.</p>
<p>The architecture answers</p>
<blockquote>
<p><strong>How are representations computed?</strong></p>
</blockquote>
<p>The objective function answers</p>
<blockquote>
<p><strong>What properties should those representations satisfy?</strong></p>
</blockquote>
<p>Once these responsibilities are separated, changing the network architecture should not fundamentally alter the optimization objective.</p>
<p>A Vision Transformer, a CNN, a text encoder, or even completely different modalities should all be trainable using the same mathematical principles.</p>
<p>The architecture simply changes the function</p>
<p><span class="katex--display"><span class="katex-display"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="block"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>f</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo>⋅</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo separator="true">,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">
f_\theta(\cdot),
</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 1em; vertical-align: -0.25em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.10764em;">f</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.336108em;"><span class="" style="top: -2.55em; margin-left: -0.10764em; margin-right: 0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mathnormal mtight" style="margin-right: 0.02778em;">θ</span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.15em;"><span class=""></span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mopen">(</span><span class="mord">⋅</span><span class="mclose">)</span><span class="mpunct">,</span></span></span></span></span></span></p>
<p>while the objective defining a “good” representation remains unchanged.</p>
<p>This is precisely what makes modularity a more fundamental formulation than previous heuristic approaches.</p>
<hr>
<p>At this point, the optimization problem has been reduced to a single unresolved question.</p>
<p>The prediction objective is already well-defined.</p>
<p>The remaining challenge is to design a regularizer</p>
<p><span class="katex--display"><span class="katex-display"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="block"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>Z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo separator="true">,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">
r(Z),
</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 1em; vertical-align: -0.25em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.02778em;">r</span><span class="mopen">(</span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.07153em;">Z</span><span class="mclose">)</span><span class="mpunct">,</span></span></span></span></span></span></p>
<p>that mathematically guarantees an embedding space cannot collapse while preserving as much information as possible.</p>
<p>The remainder of this module is devoted entirely to constructing that regularizer from first principles.</p>
<h1 id="part-5-vicreg-architecture">Part 5: VICReg Architecture</h1>
<h2 id="from-a-modular-objective-to-a-trainable-architecture">From a Modular Objective to a Trainable Architecture</h2>
<p>Part 4 established that the optimization problem naturally decomposes into two independent objectives:</p>
<ul>
<li>make different views of the same sample agree,</li>
<li>ensure each embedding space remains informative.</li>
</ul>
<p>However, an optimization objective alone is not enough.</p>
<p>We still require a neural architecture capable of producing the representations on which these objectives operate.</p>
<p>The role of the architecture is <strong>not</strong> to prevent collapse.</p>
<p>That responsibility now belongs entirely to the objective function.</p>
<p>Instead, the architecture has a much simpler purpose:</p>
<blockquote>
<p><strong>Compute representations that can be optimized by the modular objective.</strong></p>
</blockquote>
<p>This distinction is important.</p>
<p>The architecture computes the representations.</p>
<p>The loss defines what makes those representations good.</p>
<hr>
<h2 id="the-two-stage-representation-pipeline">The Two-Stage Representation Pipeline</h2>
<p>Given an input image</p>
<p><span class="katex--display"><span class="katex-display"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="block"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo separator="true">,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">
x,
</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.625em; vertical-align: -0.19444em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal">x</span><span class="mpunct">,</span></span></span></span></span></span></p>
<p>two random augmentations are generated,</p>
<p><span class="katex--display"><span class="katex-display"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="block"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>T</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo separator="true">,</mo><mspace width="2em"></mspace><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>T</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">.</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">
x_1=T_1(x),
\qquad
x_2=T_2(x).
</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.58056em; vertical-align: -0.15em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal">x</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.301108em;"><span class="" style="top: -2.55em; margin-left: 0em; margin-right: 0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight">1</span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.15em;"><span class=""></span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.277778em;"></span><span class="mrel">=</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.277778em;"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 1em; vertical-align: -0.25em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.13889em;">T</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.301108em;"><span class="" style="top: -2.55em; margin-left: -0.13889em; margin-right: 0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight">1</span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.15em;"><span class=""></span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mopen">(</span><span class="mord mathnormal">x</span><span class="mclose">)</span><span class="mpunct">,</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 2em;"></span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.166667em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal">x</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.301108em;"><span class="" style="top: -2.55em; margin-left: 0em; margin-right: 0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight">2</span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.15em;"><span class=""></span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.277778em;"></span><span class="mrel">=</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.277778em;"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 1em; vertical-align: -0.25em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.13889em;">T</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.301108em;"><span class="" style="top: -2.55em; margin-left: -0.13889em; margin-right: 0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight">2</span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.15em;"><span class=""></span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mopen">(</span><span class="mord mathnormal">x</span><span class="mclose">)</span><span class="mord">.</span></span></span></span></span></span></p>
<p>These two views are processed independently.</p>
<p>Each branch consists of two sequential stages.</p>
<pre><code>Input
   │
Encoder
   │
Representation
   │
Expander
   │
Embedding
</code></pre>
<p>The two branches may</p>
<ul>
<li>share parameters (Siamese),</li>
<li>have different parameters,</li>
<li>or even use completely different architectures.</li>
</ul>
<p>The modular objective introduced in Part 4 does not depend on this choice.</p>
<hr>
<h1 id="stage-1-—-the-encoder">Stage 1 — The Encoder</h1>
<p>The encoder performs the primary representation learning.</p>
<p>Mathematically,</p>
<p><span class="katex--display"><span class="katex-display"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="block"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>y</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>f</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo separator="true">,</mo><mspace width="2em"></mspace><msub><mi>y</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>f</mi><msup><mi>θ</mi><mo mathvariant="normal" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">′</mo></msup></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">.</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">
y_1=f_\theta(x_1),
\qquad
y_2=f_{\theta'}(x_2).
</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.625em; vertical-align: -0.19444em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.03588em;">y</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.301108em;"><span class="" style="top: -2.55em;
