margin-left: -0.03588em; margin-right: 0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight">2</span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.15em;"><span class=""></span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.277778em;"></span><span class="mrel">=</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.277778em;"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 1em; vertical-align: -0.25em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.10764em;">f</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.336108em;"><span class="" style="top: -2.55em; margin-left: -0.10764em; margin-right: 0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight"><span class="mord mtight"><span class="mord mathnormal mtight" style="margin-right: 0.02778em;">θ</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.682829em;"><span class="" style="top: -2.786em; margin-right: 0.0714286em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 2.5em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size3 size1 mtight"><span class="mord mtight"><span class="mord mtight">′</span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.15em;"><span class=""></span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mopen">(</span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal">x</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.301108em;"><span class="" style="top: -2.55em; margin-left: 0em; margin-right: 0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight">2</span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.15em;"><span class=""></span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mclose">)</span><span class="mord">.</span></span></span></span></span></span></p>
<p>The vectors</p>
<p><span class="katex--display"><span class="katex-display"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="block"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>y</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo separator="true">,</mo>  <msub><mi>y</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">
y_1,\;y_2
</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.625em; vertical-align: -0.19444em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.03588em;">y</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.301108em;"><span class="" style="top: -2.55em; margin-left: -0.03588em; margin-right: 0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight">1</span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.15em;"><span class=""></span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mpunct">,</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.277778em;"></span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.166667em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.03588em;">y</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.301108em;"><span class="" style="top: -2.55em; margin-left: -0.03588em; margin-right: 0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight">2</span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.15em;"><span class=""></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></p>
<p>are called the <strong>representations</strong>.</p>
<p>Their purpose is to encode the semantic content of the input.</p>
<p>After self-supervised pretraining is complete,</p>
<p><strong>these are the vectors that will actually be used for downstream tasks.</strong></p>
<p>The encoder therefore learns the representation we ultimately care about.</p>
<hr>
<h2 id="why-not-compute-the-loss-here">Why Not Compute the Loss Here?</h2>
<p>A natural question is</p>
<blockquote>
<p>Why not directly apply VICReg to the encoder output?</p>
</blockquote>
<p>At first glance,</p>
<p>this seems simpler.</p>
<p>However, the encoder has two competing responsibilities.</p>
<p>It must</p>
<ul>
<li>preserve semantic information useful for downstream tasks,</li>
<li>while simultaneously satisfying strong statistical constraints imposed by the self-supervised objective.</li>
</ul>
<p>These goals are not always perfectly aligned.</p>
<p>For example,</p>
<p>the regularizer may encourage the embedding coordinates to become decorrelated,</p>
<p>while the downstream task may actually benefit from retaining certain statistical dependencies.</p>
<p>If these constraints are imposed directly on the representation,</p>
<p>the encoder is forced to compromise between</p>
<p>learning useful features</p>
<p>and</p>
<p>satisfying the optimization objective.</p>
<p>Ideally,</p>
<p>we would like these two responsibilities to be separated.</p>
<hr>
<h1 id="stage-2-—-the-expander">Stage 2 — The Expander</h1>
<p>To achieve this separation,</p>
<p>the representation is passed through another network,</p>
<p>usually a multi-layer perceptron,</p>
<p>called the <strong>expander</strong> (or projection head).</p>
<p>Mathematically,</p>
<p><span class="katex--display"><span class="katex-display"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="block"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>z</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>ϕ</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo separator="true">,</mo><mspace width="2em"></mspace><msub><mi>z</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>ϕ</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">.</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">
z_1=g_\phi(y_1),
\qquad
z_2=g_\phi(y_2).
</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.58056em; vertical-align: -0.15em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.04398em;">z</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.301108em;"><span class="" style="top: -2.55em; margin-left: -0.04398em; margin-right: 0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight">1</span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.15em;"><span class=""></span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.277778em;"></span><span class="mrel">=</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.277778em;"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 1.03611em; vertical-align: -0.286108em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.03588em;">g</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.336108em;"><span class="" style="top: -2.55em; margin-left: -0.03588em; margin-right: 0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mathnormal mtight">ϕ</span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.286108em;"><span class=""></span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mopen">(</span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.03588em;">y</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.301108em;"><span class="" style="top: -2.55em; margin-left: -0.03588em; margin-right: 0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight">1</span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.15em;"><span class=""></span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mclose">)</span><span class="mpunct">,</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 2em;"></span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.166667em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.04398em;">z</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.301108em;"><span class="" style="top: -2.55em; margin-left: -0.04398em; margin-right: 0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight">2</span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.15em;"><span class=""></span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.277778em;"></span><span class="mrel">=</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.277778em;"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 1.03611em; vertical-align: -0.286108em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.03588em;">g</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.336108em;"><span class="" style="top: -2.55em; margin-left: -0.03588em; margin-right: 0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mathnormal mtight">ϕ</span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.286108em;"><span class=""></span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mopen">(</span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.03588em;">y</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.301108em;"><span class="" style="top: -2.55em; margin-left: -0.03588em; margin-right: 0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight">2</span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.15em;"><span class=""></span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mclose">)</span><span class="mord">.</span></span></span></span></span></span></p>
<p>The vectors</p>
<p><span class="katex--display"><span class="katex-display"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="block"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>z</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo separator="true">,</mo>  <msub><mi>z</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">
z_1,\;z_2
</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.625em; vertical-align: -0.19444em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.04398em;">z</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.301108em;"><span class="" style="top: -2.55em; margin-left: -0.04398em; margin-right: 0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight">1</span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.15em;"><span class=""></span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mpunct">,</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.277778em;"></span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.166667em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.04398em;">z</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.301108em;"><span class="" style="top: -2.55em; margin-left: -0.04398em; margin-right: 0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight">2</span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.15em;"><span class=""></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></p>
<p>are called the <strong>embeddings</strong>.</p>
<p>Importantly,</p>
<p><strong>every VICReg loss is computed only on these embeddings.</strong></p>
<p>The encoder output is never directly regularized.</p>
<hr>
<h2 id="why-introduce-another-network">Why Introduce Another Network?</h2>
<p>The expander serves as an intermediate optimization space.</p>
<p>Instead of forcing the encoder representation itself to satisfy every statistical constraint,</p>
<p>the expander absorbs those constraints.</p>
<p>The optimization therefore becomes</p>
<p><span class="katex--display"><span class="katex-display"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="block"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>⟶</mo><mi>z</mi><mo>⟶</mo><mi>L</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">.</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">
y
\longrightarrow
z
\longrightarrow
L.
</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.70544em; vertical-align: -0.19444em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.03588em;">y</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.277778em;"></span><span class="mrel">⟶</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.277778em;"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.522em; vertical-align: -0.011em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.04398em;">z</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.277778em;"></span><span class="mrel">⟶</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.277778em;"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.68333em; vertical-align: 0em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal">L</span><span class="mord">.</span></span></span></span></span></span></p>
<p>rather than</p>
<p><span class="katex--display"><span class="katex-display"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="block"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>⟶</mo><mi>L</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">.</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">
y
\longrightarrow
L.
</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.70544em; vertical-align: -0.19444em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.03588em;">y</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.277778em;"></span><span class="mrel">⟶</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.277778em;"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.68333em; vertical-align: 0em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal">L</span><span class="mord">.</span></span></span></span></span></span></p>
<p>This allows the encoder to focus primarily on learning semantic features,</p>
<p>while the expander learns whatever geometric transformation is necessary for the loss.</p>
<p>Once training finishes,</p>
<p>the expander is discarded.</p>
<p>Only the encoder remains.</p>
<hr>
<h2 id="why-can-we-throw-the-expander-away">Why Can We Throw the Expander Away?</h2>
<p>The expander exists only to make optimization easier.</p>
<p>Its output is never intended to become the final representation.</p>
<p>Instead,</p>
<p>the gradients flowing through the expander modify the encoder parameters,</p>
<p>allowing the encoder to learn increasingly useful representations.</p>
<p>After training,</p>
<p>the optimization objective no longer exists.</p>
<p>Only the learned encoder is needed.</p>
<p>The expander has therefore completed its purpose and can be removed without affecting inference.</p>
<hr>
<h2 id="why-expand-into-a-higher-dimensional-space">Why Expand Into a Higher-Dimensional Space?</h2>
<p>The projection head usually increases dimensionality.</p>
<p>For example,</p>
<p><span class="katex--display"><span class="katex-display"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="block"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi mathvariant="double-struck">R</mi><mn>512</mn></msup><mo>⟶</mo><msup><mi mathvariant="double-struck">R</mi><mn>2048</mn></msup><mi mathvariant="normal">.</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">
\mathbb{R}^{512}
\longrightarrow
\mathbb{R}^{2048}.
</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.875108em; vertical-align: -0.011em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathbb">R</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.864108em;"><span class="" style="top: -3.113em; margin-right: 0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight"><span class="mord mtight">512</span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.277778em;"></span><span class="mrel">⟶</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.277778em;"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.864108em; vertical-align: 0em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathbb">R</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.864108em;"><span class="" style="top: -3.113em; margin-right: 0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight"><span class="mord mtight">2048</span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mord">.</span></span></span></span></span></span></p>
<p>This is not done to store more information.</p>
<p>The encoder has already extracted the information.</p>
<p>Instead,</p>
<p>the higher-dimensional embedding provides the optimizer with greater flexibility for satisfying statistical constraints.</p>
<p>Suppose two semantic features are partially correlated.</p>
<p>A higher-dimensional nonlinear mapping can rotate, separate, and redistribute these features into a space where</p>
<ul>
<li>each coordinate maintains sufficient variance,</li>
<li>different coordinates become less redundant,</li>
<li>and the statistical regularizers are easier to satisfy.</li>
</ul>
<p>Importantly,</p>
<p>the semantic information itself is not created by the expander.</p>
<p>The expander merely reorganizes that information into a geometry more suitable for optimization.</p>
<hr>
<h2 id="separating-representation-learning-from-optimization">Separating Representation Learning from Optimization</h2>
<p>The complete architecture therefore has a clear division of responsibilities.</p>
<p>The encoder answers</p>
<blockquote>
<p><strong>What information about the input should be preserved?</strong></p>
</blockquote>
<p>The expander answers</p>
<blockquote>
<p><strong>How should that information be arranged so the optimization objective can be satisfied?</strong></p>
</blockquote>
<p>The modular loss then answers</p>
<blockquote>
<p><strong>Does this embedding space satisfy the mathematical properties required for self-supervised learning?</strong></p>
</blockquote>
<p>Each component has exactly one responsibility.</p>
<p>This separation is one of the central design principles behind VICReg.</p>
<hr>
<p>The architecture is now fully specified.</p>
<p>The remaining task is to determine <strong>what statistical properties the embedding vectors</strong></p>
<p><span class="katex--display"><span class="katex-display"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="block"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>z</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo separator="true">,</mo><mspace width="2em"></mspace><msub><mi>z</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">
z_1,\qquad
z_2
</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.625em; vertical-align: -0.19444em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.04398em;">z</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.301108em;"><span class="" style="top: -2.55em; margin-left: -0.04398em; margin-right: 0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight">1</span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.15em;"><span class=""></span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mpunct">,</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 2em;"></span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.166667em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.04398em;">z</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.301108em;"><span class="" style="top: -2.55em; margin-left: -0.04398em; margin-right: 0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight">2</span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.15em;"><span class=""></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></p>
<p><strong>must satisfy in order to guarantee non-collapsed, information-rich representations.</strong></p>
<p>The next parts derive these statistical constraints one by one.</p>
<h3 id="part-6-invariance--variance-mechanics">Part 6: Invariance &amp; Variance Mechanics</h3>
<p><strong>1. The Invariance Term (The Attraction Force)</strong> The primary objective of the architecture is to learn representations that remain consistent across different augmented views of the same underlying data. <h3 id="what-is-l_2-normalization">What is <span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>L</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L_2</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.83333em; vertical-align: -0.15em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal">L</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.301108em;"><span class="" style="top: -2.55em; margin-left: 0em; margin-right: 0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight">2</span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.15em;"><span class=""></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span> Normalization?</h3>
<p>Mathematically, <span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>L</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L_2</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.83333em; vertical-align: -0.15em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal">L</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.301108em;"><span class="" style="top: -2.55em; margin-left: 0em; margin-right: 0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight">2</span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.15em;"><span class=""></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span> normalization takes a vector and divides it by its own Euclidean length (magnitude):</p>
<p><span class="katex--display"><span class="katex-display"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="block"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>z</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>r</mi><mi>m</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mi>z</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">∣</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∣</mi><mi>z</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∣</mi><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">∣</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z_{norm} = \frac{z}{||z||_2}</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.58056em; vertical-align: -0.936em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mopen nulldelimiter"></span><span class="mfrac"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 1.10756em;"><span class="" style="top: -2.314em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 3em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord">∣∣</span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.04398em;">z</span><span class="mord">∣</span><span class="mord"><span class="mord">∣</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.301108em;"><span class="" style="top: -2.55em; margin-left: 0em; margin-right: 0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight">2</span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.15em;"><span class=""></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="" style="top: -3.23em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 3em;"></span><span class="frac-line" style="border-bottom-width: 0.04em;"></span></span><span class="" style="top: -3.677em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 3em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.04398em;">z</span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.936em;"><span class=""></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mclose nulldelimiter"></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></p>
<p>Geometrically, if you think of your latent space as a 3D room, <span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>L</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L_2</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.83333em; vertical-align: -0.15em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal">L</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.301108em;"><span class="" style="top: -2.55em; margin-left: 0em; margin-right: 0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight">2</span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.15em;"><span class=""></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span> normalization takes every single data point in that room and projects it onto the surface of a sphere with a radius of 1 (a unit hypersphere). It completely strips away the <em>length</em> of the vector, leaving only its <em>direction</em>.</p>
<h3 id="why-contrastive-and-cosine-methods-rely-on-it">Why Contrastive and Cosine Methods Rely on It</h3>
<p>In contrastive learning (like SimCLR or MoCo), the network learns by measuring the angle between vectors.</p>
<ul>
<li>
<p><strong>How it’s used:</strong> The similarity between two embeddings is computed using the dot product: <span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>s</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><msubsup><mi>z</mi><mi>i</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">⊤</mi></msubsup><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>j</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s_{ij} = z_i^\top z_j</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.716668em; vertical-align: -0.286108em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal">s</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.311664em;"><span class="" style="top: -2.55em; margin-left: 0em; margin-right: 0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight"><span class="mord mathnormal mtight" style="margin-right: 0.05724em;">ij</span></span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.286108em;"><span class=""></span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.277778em;"></span><span class="mrel">=</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.277778em;"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 1.13522em; vertical-align: -0.286108em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.04398em;">z</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.849108em;"><span class="" style="top: -2.44134em; margin-left: -0.04398em; margin-right: 0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mathnormal mtight">i</span></span></span><span class="" style="top: -3.063em; margin-right: 0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight">⊤</span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.258664em;"><span class=""></span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.04398em;">z</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.311664em;"><span class="" style="top: -2.55em; margin-left: -0.04398em; margin-right: 0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mathnormal mtight" style="margin-right: 0.05724em;">j</span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.286108em;"><span class=""></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span>. If both vectors are already <span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>L</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L_2</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.83333em; vertical-align: -0.15em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal">L</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.301108em;"><span class="" style="top: -2.55em; margin-left: 0em; margin-right: 0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight">2</span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.15em;"><span class=""></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span> normalized (meaning their length is exactly 1), this dot product mathematically simplifies to exactly the cosine of the angle between them (<span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>c</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">cos(\theta)</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 1em; vertical-align: -0.25em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal">cos</span><span class="mopen">(</span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.02778em;">θ</span><span class="mclose">)</span></span></span></span></span>).</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><strong>Why it’s necessary:</strong> Contrastive methods use a loss function (like InfoNCE) that compares the similarity of a positive pair against thousands of negative pairs. If vectors were allowed to have different lengths, a negative sample with a massive magnitude could artificially inflate its dot product, completely overpowering the loss function and destroying the training stability.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>By forcing everything onto the unit sphere, the network puts every embedding on an equal playing field. It forces the model to encode all semantic meaning <em>purely in the direction</em> the vector is pointing. It also guarantees that similarity scores strictly stay between -1 and 1, which keeps the gradients stable.</p>
</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="why-vicreg-abandons-normalization">Why VICReg Abandons Normalization</h3>
<p>VICReg operates on an entirely different philosophy. As the text states, VICReg computes its invariance distance without normalization because it needs to interact directly with the <strong>Variance</strong> regularizer.</p>
<ul>
<li>
<p><strong>The Geometric Trap:</strong> VICReg prevents collapse by forcing the points to spread out. The Variance term explicitly demands that the standard deviation of each dimension reaches a target threshold <span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>γ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.625em; vertical-align: -0.19444em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.05556em;">γ</span></span></span></span></span> (typically <span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>γ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma = 1</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.625em; vertical-align: -0.19444em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.05556em;">γ</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.277778em;"></span><span class="mrel">=</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.277778em;"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.64444em; vertical-align: 0em;"></span><span class="mord">1</span></span></span></span></span>).</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>If you applied <span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>L</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L_2</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.83333em; vertical-align: -0.15em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal">L</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.301108em;"><span class="" style="top: -2.55em; margin-left: 0em; margin-right: 0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight">2</span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.15em;"><span class=""></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span> normalization to the embeddings <em>before</em> calculating the VICReg loss, you would trap all your data points on the rigid, curved shell of the unit sphere.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>By trapping the points on a sphere, you artificially restrict their variance. The optimizer would try to push the points apart to hit that target <span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>γ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma=1</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.625em; vertical-align: -0.19444em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.05556em;">γ</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.277778em;"></span><span class="mrel">=</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.277778em;"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.64444em; vertical-align: 0em;"></span><span class="mord">1</span></span></span></span></span> threshold, but the normalization step would constantly snap them back to the sphere’s surface. The geometric curvature of the sphere limits how statistically independent and spread out the variables can actually become.</p>
</li>
</ul>
<p>By completely abandoning <span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>L</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L_2</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.83333em; vertical-align: -0.15em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal">L</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.301108em;"><span class="" style="top: -2.55em; margin-left: 0em; margin-right: 0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight">2</span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.15em;"><span class=""></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span> normalization, VICReg allows the embeddings to detach from the sphere and occupy the entire, unrestricted volume of the latent space. This gives the network the mathematical freedom to scale, stretch, and distribute the points radially to perfectly satisfy the Variance and Covariance rules.<br>
<strong>2. The Variance Term (The Repulsion Force)</strong> If the network only minimized <span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>Z</mi><mo separator="true">,</mo><msup><mi>Z</mi><mo mathvariant="normal" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">′</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s(Z, Z')</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 1.00189em; vertical-align: -0.25em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal">s</span><span class="mopen">(</span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.07153em;">Z</span><span class="mpunct">,</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.166667em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.07153em;">Z</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.751892em;"><span class="" style="top: -3.063em; margin-right: 0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight"><span class="mord mtight">′</span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mclose">)</span></span></span></span></span>, it would suffer complete topological collapse, mapping all inputs to a constant vector to achieve a distance of exactly zero. To explicitly prevent this, VICReg introduces a hinge loss to maintain the spread of the embeddings over the batch.</p>
<p>Let <span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>z</mi><mi>j</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z^j</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.824664em; vertical-align: 0em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.04398em;">z</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.824664em;"><span class="" style="top: -3.063em; vertical-align: -0.19444em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.05724em;">j</span></span></span></span></span> across all <span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.43056em; vertical-align: 0em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal">n</span></span></span></span></span> vectors in the batch <span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>Z</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Z</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.68333em; vertical-align: 0em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.07153em;">Z</span></span></span></span></span>. The variance regularization term <span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>Z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v(Z)</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 1em; This term forces the embedding vectors of different samples within the batch to spread out, explicitly preventing the norm of the vectors from shrinking to zero.</p>
<p><strong>The Gradient Velocity Insight: Why Standard Deviation?</strong> A crucial mathematical nuance is the use of the standard deviation <span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><msqrt><mrow><mtext>Var</mtext><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msqrt></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sqrt{\text{Var}(x)}</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 1.24em; vertical-align: -0.305em;"></span><span class="mord sqrt"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.935em;"><span class="svg-align" style="top: -3.2em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 3.2em;"></span><span class="mord" style="padding-left: 1em;"><span class="mord text"><span class="mord">Var</span></span><span class="mopen">(</span><span class="mord mathnormal">x</span><span class="mclose">)</span></span></span><span class="" style="top: -2.895em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 3.2em;"></span><span class="hide-tail" style="min-width: 1.02em; height: 1.28em;"><svg width="400em" height="1.28em" viewBox="0 0 400000 1296" preserveAspectRatio="xMinYMin slice"><path d="M263,681c0.7,0,18,39.7,52,119

M1001 80h400000v40h-400000z"></path></svg></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.305em;"><span class=""></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span> rather than the raw variance <span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mtext>Var</mtext><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\text{Var}(x)</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 1em; vertical-align: -0.25em;"></span><span class="mord text"><span class="mord">Var</span></span><span class="mopen">(</span><span class="mord mathnormal">x</span><span class="mclose">)</span></span></span></span></span> inside the hinge function.</p>
<p>If the raw variance were used, the gradient of the loss with respect to the embeddings would become vanishingly small as the actual variance approached the target threshold <span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>γ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.625em; vertical-align: -0.19444em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.05556em;">γ</span></span></span></span></span>. Consequently, the corrective “repulsive” force would drop to near zero right at the boundary of collapse, failing to push the vectors apart effectively. By using the standard deviation, the gradient maintains a robust, constant magnitude even as it approaches the threshold, ensuring a reliable escape velocity from complete collapse.</p>
<p>Are you ready to move to Part 7, where we introduce the final piece of the VICReg triad—Covariance Regularization—and see how it prevents the more insidious dimensional collapse?<br>
Let’s strip away the Greek letters and look at what this equation is actually doing physically in the latent space.</p>
<h3 id="what-is-a-hinge-loss">1. What is a “Hinge Loss”?</h3>
<p>In machine learning, a <strong>hinge loss</strong> is essentially a mathematical bouncer. It enforces a strict boundary, but once you cross that boundary, it stops caring about you entirely.</p>
<p>The core of a hinge loss looks like this: <span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>max</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo separator="true">,</mo><mtext>Target</mtext><mo>−</mo><mtext>Current&nbsp;Value</mtext><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\max(0, \text{Target} - \text{Current Value})</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 1em; vertical-align: -0.25em;"></span><span class="mop">max</span><span class="mopen">(</span><span class="mord">0</span><span class="mpunct">,</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.166667em;"></span><span class="mord text"><span class="mord">Target</span></span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.222222em;"></span><span class="mbin">−</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.222222em;"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 1em; vertical-align: -0.25em;"></span><span class="mord text"><span class="mord">Current&nbsp;Value</span></span><span class="mclose">)</span></span></span></span></span></p>
<ul>
<li>
<p><strong>If you are below the target:</strong> The math results in a positive number. This is your “penalty” (loss). The network gets punished and has to change its weights to fix it.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><strong>If you meet or exceed the target:</strong> The math results in zero or a negative number. Because of the <span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>max</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo separator="true">,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">.</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">.</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">.</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\max(0, ...)</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 1em; vertical-align: -0.25em;"></span><span class="mop">max</span><span class="mopen">(</span><span class="mord">0</span><span class="mpunct">,</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.166667em;"></span><span class="mord">...</span><span class="mclose">)</span></span></span></span></span> function, the loss just becomes exactly 0. The penalty turns off.</p>
</li>
</ul>
<p><strong>Geometrically:</strong> Imagine you are blowing up a balloon inside a rigid box. The hinge loss is the walls of the box. As long as the balloon is smaller than the box, you have to keep blowing (pushing outward). The exact moment the balloon touches the walls, you stop. If you try to make it even bigger, the loss function doesn’t care; it just wants you to hit that minimum size.</p>
<h3 id="breaking-down-the-variance-equation">2. Breaking Down the Variance Equation</h3>
<p>Here is the exact equation from the text:</p>
<p><span class="katex--display"><span class="katex-display"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="block"><semantics><mrow><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>Z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>d</mi></mfrac><munderover><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>d</mi></munderover><mi>max</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo separator="true">,</mo><mi>γ</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>S</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>z</mi><mi>j</mi></msup><mo separator="true">,</mo><mi>ϵ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v(Z) = \frac{1}{d} \sum_{j=1}^{d} \max(0, \gamma - S(z^j, \epsilon))</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 1em; margin-right: 0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mathnormal mtight" style="margin-right: 0.05724em;">j</span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mpunct">,</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.166667em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal">ϵ</span><span class="mclose">))</span></span></span></span></span></span></p>
<p>Let’s translate this into plain English, piece by piece:</p>
<ul>
<li>
<p><strong><span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>d</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.69444em; vertical-align: 0em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal">d</span></span></span></span></span></strong>: This is the number of dimensions in your room (e.g., the X, Y, and Z axes).</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><strong><span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>d</mi></mfrac><msubsup><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>d</mi></msubsup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{d} \sum_{j=1}^{d}</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 1.42483em; margin-right: 0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight"><span class="mord mathnormal mtight" style="margin-right: 0.05724em;">j</span><span class="mrel mtight">=</span><span class="mord mtight">1</span></span></span></span><span class="" style="top: -3.2029em; margin-right: 0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight"><span class="mord mathnormal mtight">d</span></span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.435818em;"><span class=""></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></strong>: This just means “calculate this rule for every single axis independently, and then average the results.”</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><strong><span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>γ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.625em; vertical-align: -0.19444em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.05556em;">γ</span></span></span></span></span> (Gamma)</strong>: This is your target threshold (the size of the box). It is usually set to <strong>1</strong>.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><strong><span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>z</mi><mi>j</mi></msup><mo separator="true">,</mo><mi>ϵ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S(z^j, \epsilon)</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 1.07466em; vertical-align: -0.25em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.05764em;">S</span><span class="mopen">(</span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.04398em;">z</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.824664em;"><span class="" style="top: -3.063em; margin-right: 0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mathnormal mtight" style="margin-right: 0.05724em;">j</span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mpunct">,</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.166667em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal">ϵ</span><span class="mclose">)</span></span></span></span></span></strong>: This is the actual, current spread (standard deviation) of all your data points along one specific axis.</p>
</li>
</ul>
<p><strong>What it means all together:</strong> The network looks at the X-axis. It asks, <em>“Are the data points spread out by at least a distance of 1?”</em> If they are only spread out by 0.2, the hinge loss kicks in and physically repels the points outward along the X-axis until the spread hits 1. Then it checks the Y-axis and does the exact same thing.</p>
<h3 id="why-is-epsilon-epsilon-there">3. Why is <span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>ϵ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\epsilon</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.43056em; vertical-align: 0em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal">ϵ</span></span></span></span></span> (Epsilon) there?</h3>
<p>Epsilon is a tiny number (like 0.0001) added purely as a mathematical safety net. It exists to prevent your computer from crashing.</p>
<p>To calculate the standard deviation <span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>S</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.68333em; vertical-align: 0em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.05764em;">S</span></span></span></span></span>, you have to take a square root:</p>
<p><span class="katex--display"><span class="katex-display"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="block"><semantics><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo separator="true">,</mo><mi>ϵ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><msqrt><mrow><mtext>Var</mtext><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>+</mo><mi>ϵ</mi></mrow></msqrt></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S(x, \epsilon) = \sqrt{\text{Var}(x) + \epsilon}</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 1em; vertical-align: -0.25em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.05764em;">S</span><span class="mopen">(</span><span class="mord mathnormal">x</span><span class="mpunct">,</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.166667em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal">ϵ</span><span class="mclose">)</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.277778em;"></span><span class="mrel">=</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.277778em;"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 1.24em; vertical-align: -0.256125em;"></span><span class="mord sqrt"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.983875em;"><span class="svg-align" style="top: -3.2em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 3.2em;"></span><span class="mord" style="padding-left: 1em;"><span class="mord text"><span class="mord">Var</span></span><span class="mopen">(</span><span class="mord mathnormal">x</span><span class="mclose">)</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.222222em;"></span><span class="mbin">+</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.222222em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal">ϵ</span></span></span><span class="" style="top: -2.94388em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 3.2em;"></span><span class="hide-tail" style="min-width: 1.02em; <p>To train the network, the optimizer has to calculate the gradient (the derivative) of this function. The derivative of a square root <span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><msqrt><mi>x</mi></msqrt></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sqrt{x}</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 1.04em; vertical-align: -0.23972em;"></span><span class="mord sqrt"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.80028em;"><span class="svg-align" style="top: -3em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 3em;"></span><span class="mord" style="padding-left: 0.833em;"><span class="mord mathnormal">x</span></span></span><span class="" style="top: -2.76028em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 3em;"></span><span class="hide-tail" style="min-width: 0.853em; height: 1.08em;"><svg width="400em" height="1.08em" viewBox="0 0 400000 1080" preserveAspectRatio="xMinYMin slice"><path d="M95,702

M834 80h400000v40h-400000z"></path></svg></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.23972em;"><span class=""></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span> is <span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mn>2</mn><msqrt><mi>x</mi></msqrt></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{2\sqrt{x}}</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 1.38311em; vertical-align: -0.538em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mopen nulldelimiter"></span><span class="mfrac"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.845108em;"><span class="" style="top: -2.62587em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 3em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight"><span class="mord mtight">2</span><span class="mord sqrt mtight"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.805905em;"><span class="svg-align" style="top: -3em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 3em;"></span><span class="mord mtight" style="padding-left: 0.833em;"><span class="mord mathnormal mtight">x</span></span></span><span class="" style="top: -2.76591em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 3em;"></span><span class="hide-tail mtight" style="min-width: 0.853em; height: 1.08em;"><svg width="400em" height="1.08em" viewBox="0 0 400000 1080" preserveAspectRatio="xMinYMin slice"><path d="M95,702

M834 80h400000v40h-400000z"></path></svg></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.234095em;"><span class=""></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="" style="top: -3.23em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 3em;"></span><span class="frac-line" style="border-bottom-width: 0.04em;"></span></span><span class="" style="top: -3.394em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 3em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight"><span class="mord mtight">1</span></span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.538em;"><span class=""></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mclose nulldelimiter"></span></span></span></span></span></span>.</p>
<p>If the network is super lazy and perfectly collapses all data points onto a single pixel, the variance becomes exactly <strong>0</strong>. If there was no epsilon, the derivative would try to calculate <span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>0</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{0}</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 1.19011em; vertical-align: -0.345em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mopen nulldelimiter"></span><span class="mfrac"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.845108em;"><span class="" style="top: -2.655em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 3em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight"><span class="mord mtight">0</span></span></span></span><span class="" style="top: -3.23em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 3em;"></span><span class="frac-line" style="border-bottom-width: 0.04em;"></span></span><span class="" style="top: -3.394em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 3em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight"><span class="mord mtight">1</span></span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.345em;"><span class=""></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mclose nulldelimiter"></span></span></span></span></span></span>. This causes a “Divide by Zero” error, your gradients explode to infinity (NaNs), and your entire training run crashes. Adding that tiny <span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>ϵ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\epsilon</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.43056em; vertical-align: 0em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal">ϵ</span></span></span></span></span> ensures the number inside the square root is never mathematically zero.</p>
<h3 id="a-complete-geometric-example">4. A Complete Geometric Example</h3>
<p>Let’s put it all together in a 2D space (just an X-axis and a Y-axis).</p>
<p><strong>The Setup:</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>
<p>You have a batch of 100 images.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Your target spread (<span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>γ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.625em; vertical-align: -0.19444em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.05556em;">γ</span></span></span></span></span>) is <strong>1</strong>.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>The network starts out lazy. It maps all 100 images to the exact same coordinate: (0, 0).</p>
</li>
</ul>
<p><strong>Step 1: The Measurement</strong></p>
<p>The loss function measures the spread on the X-axis. Since all points are at 0, the spread is 0.</p>
<p>The hinge loss calculates: <span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>max</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo separator="true">,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\max(0, 1 - 0) = 1</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 1em; vertical-align: -0.25em;"></span><span class="mop">max</span><span class="mopen">(</span><span class="mord">0</span><span class="mpunct">,</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.166667em;"></span><span class="mord">1</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.222222em;"></span><span class="mbin">−</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.222222em;"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 1em; vertical-align: -0.25em;"></span><span class="mord">0</span><span class="mclose">)</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.277778em;"></span><span class="mrel">=</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.277778em;"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.64444em; vertical-align: 0em;"></span><span class="mord">1</span></span></span></span></span>.</p>
<p>There is a massive penalty!</p>
<p><strong>Step 2: The Repulsion</strong></p>
<p>Because of that penalty, a repulsive force field turns on. The gradients push the 100 points away from each other along the X-axis and Y-axis.</p>
<p><strong>Step 3: The Boundary</strong></p>
<p>The points start scattering outward like a cloud.</p>
<ul>
<li>
<p>Eventually, the spread of the cloud along the X-axis hits 1. The hinge loss for the X-axis becomes <span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>max</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo separator="true">,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\max(0, 1 - 1) = 0</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 1em; vertical-align: -0.25em;"></span><span class="mop">max</span><span class="mopen">(</span><span class="mord">0</span><span class="mpunct">,</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.166667em;"></span><span class="mord">1</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.222222em;"></span><span class="mbin">−</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.222222em;"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 1em; vertical-align: -0.25em;"></span><span class="mord">1</span><span class="mclose">)</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.277778em;"></span><span class="mrel">=</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.277778em;"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.64444em; vertical-align: 0em;"></span><span class="mord">0</span></span></span></span></span>. The pushing force on the X-axis shuts off.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>The spread on the Y-axis hits 1. The hinge loss for the Y-axis becomes 0. The pushing force on the Y-axis shuts off.</p>
</li>
</ul>
<p>The data points are now safely hovering in a healthy, spread-out cloud. The network successfully escaped the “collapse,” and because it used a hinge loss, it won’t waste energy pushing the points infinitely far away—it just pushed them exactly as far as necessary to be mathematically distinct.</p>
<p>Got it. No more analogies. Here is the rigorous calculus of the gradient dynamics during a topological collapse, and exactly why the square root mathematically prevents the optimization from stalling.</p>
<h3 id="the-raw-variance-derivative-the-vanishing-gradient">1. The Raw Variance Derivative (The Vanishing Gradient)</h3>
<p>Let <span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>V</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">V</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.68333em; vertical-align: 0em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.22222em;">V</span></span></span></span></span> be the empirical variance of a batch of embeddings <span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>Z</mi><mo>=</mo><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo separator="true">,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">.</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">.</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">.</mi><mo separator="true">,</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Z = \{z_1, ..., z_n\}</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.68333em; vertical-align: 0em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.07153em;">Z</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.277778em;"></span><span class="mrel">=</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.277778em;"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 1em; vertical-align: -0.25em;"></span><span class="mopen">{</span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.04398em;">z</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.301108em;"><span class="" style="top: -2.55em; margin-left: -0.04398em; margin-right: 0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight">1</span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.15em;"><span class=""></span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mpunct">,</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.166667em;"></span><span class="mord">...</span><span class="mpunct">,</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.166667em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.04398em;">z</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.151392em;"><span class="" style="top: -2.55em; margin-left: -0.04398em; margin-right: 0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mathnormal mtight">n</span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.15em;"><span class=""></span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mclose">}</span></span></span></span></span> for a single dimension. Assuming the batch is mean-centered, the variance is:</p>

<p>If the loss function used raw variance, the hinge loss in the collapse regime (where the variance is below the threshold <span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>γ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.625em; vertical-align: -0.19444em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.05556em;">γ</span></span></span></span></span>) is:</p>

<p>The gradient magnitude decays linearly with the feature scale. When the network is collapsed, the gradient vanishes to exactly <span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.64444em; vertical-align: 0em;"></span><span class="mord">0</span></span></span></span></span>. The optimizer receives no corrective signal, and the architecture is permanently trapped in the degenerate state.</p>
<h3 id="the-standard-deviation-derivative-the-constant-gradient">2. The Standard Deviation Derivative (The Constant Gradient)</h3>
<p>VICReg uses the regularized standard deviation <span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>=</mo><msqrt><mrow><mi>V</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>ϵ</mi></mrow></msqrt></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S = \sqrt{V + \epsilon}</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.68333em; vertical-align: 0em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.05764em;">S</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.277778em;"></span><span class="mrel">=</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.277778em;"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 1.04em; vertical-align: -0.155em;"></span><span class="mord sqrt"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.885em;"><span class="svg-align" style="top: -3em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 3em;"></span><span class="mord" style="padding-left: 0.833em;"><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.22222em;">V</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.222222em;"></span><span class="mbin">+</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.222222em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal">ϵ</span></span></span><span class="" style="top: -2.845em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 3em;"></span><span class="hide-tail" style="min-width: 0.853em; height: 1.08em;"><svg width="400em" height="1.08em" viewBox="0 0 400000 1080" preserveAspectRatio="xMinYMin slice"><path d="M95,702
