margin-left: 0em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 3.05em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight"><span class="mord mathnormal mtight" style="margin-right: 0.03148em;">k</span><span class="mrel mtight">=</span><span class="mord mtight">1</span></span></span></span><span class="" style="top: -3.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 3.05em;"></span><span class=""><span class="mop op-symbol large-op">∑</span></span></span><span class="" style="top: -4.3em; margin-left: 0em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 3.05em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight"><span class="mord mathnormal mtight" style="margin-right: 0.07153em;">K</span></span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 1.30211em;"><span class=""></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.166667em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal">λ</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.336108em;"><span class="" style="top: -2.55em; margin-left: 0em; margin-right: 0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mathnormal mtight" style="margin-right: 0.03148em;">k</span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.15em;"><span class=""></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></p>
<p>The trace measures the total amount of variation present in the embedding cloud.</p>
<p>An intuitive analogy is to imagine a fixed amount of water.</p>
<p>The total amount of water never changes.</p>
<p>The only question is how that water is distributed among several containers.</p>
<p>Likewise,</p>
<p>the total variance remains fixed.</p>
<p>Only its distribution across different latent directions changes.</p>
<hr>
<h1 id="what-eigenvalues-actually-represent">What Eigenvalues Actually Represent</h1>
<p>The covariance matrix tells us how the embedding cloud spreads through latent space.</p>
<p>Its eigenvectors define the principal directions along which the cloud varies.</p>
<p>Its eigenvalues measure <strong>how much</strong> variation exists along each of those directions.</p>
<p>Imagine performing Principal Component Analysis (PCA).</p>
<p>PCA rotates the coordinate system so that every new axis captures an independent direction of variation.</p>
<p>Along each axis,</p>
<p>one number tells us how wide the cloud is.</p>
<p>That number is the eigenvalue.</p>
<p>Large eigenvalue</p>
<ul>
<li>wide spread,</li>
<li>many distinguishable samples,</li>
<li>rich information along that direction.</li>
</ul>
<p>Small eigenvalue</p>
<ul>
<li>narrow spread,</li>
<li>samples nearly overlap,</li>
<li>little usable information.</li>
</ul>
<p>An eigenvalue therefore measures the “capacity” of one independent direction in the representation.</p>
<hr>
<h1 id="isotropic-and-anisotropic-geometry">Isotropic And Anisotropic Geometry</h1>
<p>Suppose the total variance equals</p>
<p><span class="katex--display"><span class="katex-display"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="block"><semantics><mrow><mn>10.</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">
10.
</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.64444em; vertical-align: 0em;"></span><span class="mord">10.</span></span></span></span></span></span></p>
<p>An isotropic embedding might have eigenvalues</p>
<p><span class="katex--display"><span class="katex-display"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="block"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo separator="true">,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo separator="true">,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo separator="true">,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo separator="true">,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">.</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">
(2,2,2,2,2).
</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 1em; vertical-align: -0.25em;"></span><span class="mopen">(</span><span class="mord">2</span><span class="mpunct">,</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.166667em;"></span><span class="mord">2</span><span class="mpunct">,</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.166667em;"></span><span class="mord">2</span><span class="mpunct">,</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.166667em;"></span><span class="mord">2</span><span class="mpunct">,</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.166667em;"></span><span class="mord">2</span><span class="mclose">)</span><span class="mord">.</span></span></span></span></span></span></p>
<p>Every direction carries exactly the same amount of information.</p>
<p>The cloud resembles a sphere.</p>
<p>Now consider</p>
<p><span class="katex--display"><span class="katex-display"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="block"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>6</mn><mo separator="true">,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo separator="true">,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo separator="true">,</mo><mn>0.7</mn><mo separator="true">,</mo><mn>0.3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">.</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">
(6,2,1,0.7,0.3).
</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 1em; vertical-align: -0.25em;"></span><span class="mopen">(</span><span class="mord">6</span><span class="mpunct">,</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.166667em;"></span><span class="mord">2</span><span class="mpunct">,</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.166667em;"></span><span class="mord">1</span><span class="mpunct">,</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.166667em;"></span><span class="mord">0.7</span><span class="mpunct">,</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.166667em;"></span><span class="mord">0.3</span><span class="mclose">)</span><span class="mord">.</span></span></span></span></span></span></p>
<p>The total variance is still</p>
<p><span class="katex--display"><span class="katex-display"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="block"><semantics><mrow><mn>10</mn><mo separator="true">,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">
10,
</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.83888em; vertical-align: -0.19444em;"></span><span class="mord">10</span><span class="mpunct">,</span></span></span></span></span></span></p>
<p>but now almost all information has been concentrated into one direction.</p>
<p>The cloud becomes elongated.</p>
<p>Some directions become extremely narrow.</p>
<p>This is called an <strong>anisotropic</strong> representation.</p>
<p>Notice that both representations contain exactly the same total variance.</p>
<p>The difference lies only in how that variance has been allocated.</p>
<hr>
<h1 id="why-narrow-directions-are-dangerous">Why Narrow Directions Are Dangerous</h1>
<p>Imagine trying to identify people using facial embeddings.</p>
<p>Suppose one latent direction corresponds to</p>
<p>“eye shape.”</p>
<p>Another corresponds to</p>
<p>“mouth shape.”</p>
<p>If the embedding allocates almost zero variance to eye shape,</p>
<p>then every person’s eye representation becomes nearly identical.</p>
<p>Although eye shape may genuinely matter for some downstream task,</p>
<p>the representation has compressed that information into an extremely narrow direction.</p>
<p>Recovering it later becomes difficult.</p>
<p>In contrast,</p>
<p>if every direction possesses similar variance,</p>
<p>no semantic factor has been excessively compressed.</p>
<p>Every downstream learner receives approximately equal access to every latent direction.</p>
<hr>
<h1 id="why-the-downstream-model-depends-on-eigenvalues">Why The Downstream Model Depends On Eigenvalues</h1>
<p>Recall from Part 10 that the linear probe predicts</p>
<p><span class="katex--display"><span class="katex-display"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="block"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>y</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>=</mo><mi>Z</mi><mi>β</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{y} = Z\beta</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.88888em; vertical-align: -0.19444em;"></span><span class="mord accent"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.69444em;"><span class="" style="top: -3em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 3em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.03588em;">y</span></span><span class="" style="top: -3em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 3em;"></span><span class="accent-body" style="left: -0.19444em;"><span class="mord">^</span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.19444em;"><span class=""></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.277778em;"></span><span class="mrel">=</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.277778em;"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.88888em; vertical-align: -0.19444em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.05278em;">Zβ</span></span></span></span></span></span></p>
<p>Everything the probe learns comes from the embedding matrix</p>
<p><span class="katex--display"><span class="katex-display"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="block"><semantics><mrow><mi>Z</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">.</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">
Z.
</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.68333em; vertical-align: 0em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.07153em;">Z</span><span class="mord">.</span></span></span></span></span></span></p>
<p>The covariance matrix</p>
<p><span class="katex--display"><span class="katex-display"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="block"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>Z</mi><mi>T</mi></msup><mi>Z</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">
Z^TZ
</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.891331em; vertical-align: 0em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.07153em;">Z</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.891331em;"><span class="" style="top: -3.113em; margin-right: 0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mathnormal mtight" style="margin-right: 0.13889em;">T</span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.07153em;">Z</span></span></span></span></span></span></p>
<p>describes how information is distributed throughout those embeddings.</p>
<p>Consequently,</p>
<p>the eigenvalues of</p>
<p><span class="katex--display"><span class="katex-display"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="block"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>Z</mi><mi>T</mi></msup><mi>Z</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">
Z^TZ
</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.891331em; vertical-align: 0em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.07153em;">Z</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.891331em;"><span class="" style="top: -3.113em; margin-right: 0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mathnormal mtight" style="margin-right: 0.13889em;">T</span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.07153em;">Z</span></span></span></span></span></span></p>
<p>determine how much usable information exists along every independent direction.</p>
<p>Changing those eigenvalues therefore changes how difficult the downstream estimation problem becomes.</p>
<p>This is why Part 11 studies the covariance spectrum rather than the raw embeddings themselves.</p>
<p>The spectrum captures the intrinsic geometry of the latent space.</p>
<hr>
<h1 id="why-we-suddenly-study-bias-and-variance">Why We Suddenly Study Bias And Variance</h1>
<p>At this point the question is no longer</p>
<blockquote>
<p>Which geometry looks nicer?</p>
</blockquote>
<p>Instead it becomes</p>
<blockquote>
<p>Which geometry produces better predictions?</p>
</blockquote>
<p>Statistical learning theory answers this using two quantities.</p>
<p>The first is <strong>bias</strong>.</p>
<p>Bias measures systematic error.</p>
<p>If we repeatedly trained the model on infinitely many datasets,</p>
<p>would the average prediction still differ from the true function?</p>
<p>If yes,</p>
<p>the estimator is biased.</p>
<p>The second is <strong>variance</strong>.</p>
<p>Variance measures instability.</p>
<p>If we trained on slightly different datasets,</p>
<p>would the learned model change dramatically?</p>
<p>If yes,</p>
<p>the estimator has high variance.</p>
<p>These two quantities summarize the fundamental sources of estimation error.</p>
<p>Changing the geometry of the embedding space changes both.</p>
<p>Therefore,</p>
<p>to compare two geometries,</p>
<p>we compare their bias and variance.</p>
<hr>
<h1 id="why-we-analyze-ridge-regression-first">Why We Analyze Ridge Regression First</h1>
<p>The notes begin with Ridge regression instead of Ordinary Least Squares because Ridge exposes the effect of anisotropy much more clearly.</p>
<p>Recall the Ridge objective,</p>
<p><span class="katex--display"><span class="katex-display"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="block"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>β</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>=</mo><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">arg min</mi><mo>⁡</mo></mrow><mi>β</mi></msub><mrow><mo fence="true">(</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∥</mi><mi>y</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>Z</mi><mi>β</mi><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">∥</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>λ</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">w</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">d</mi></mrow></msub><mi mathvariant="normal">∥</mi><mi>β</mi><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">∥</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo fence="true">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\beta} = \operatorname{arg\,min}_{\beta} \left( \|y - Z\beta\|^2 + \lambda_{\mathrm{wd}}\|\beta\|^2 \right)</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 1.15232em; vertical-align: -0.19444em;"></span><span class="mord accent"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.95788em;"><span class="" style="top: -3em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 3em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.05278em;">β</span></span><span class="" style="top: -3.26344em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 3em;"></span><span class="accent-body" style="left: -0.16666em;"><span class="mord">^</span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.19444em;"><span class=""></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.277778em;"></span><span class="mrel">=</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.277778em;"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 1.24436em; vertical-align: -0.380248em;"></span><span class="mop"><span class="mop"><span class="mord mathrm" style="margin-right: 0.01389em;">arg</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.166667em;"></span><span class="mord mathrm">min</span></span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.241968em;"><span class="" style="top: -2.45586em; margin-right: 0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight"><span class="mord mathnormal mtight" style="margin-right: 0.05278em;">β</span></span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.380248em;"><span class=""></span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.166667em;"></span><span class="minner"><span class="mopen delimcenter" style="top: 0em;"><span class="delimsizing size1">(</span></span><span class="mord">∥</span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.03588em;">y</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.222222em;"></span><span class="mbin">−</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.222222em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.05278em;">Zβ</span><span class="mord"><span class="mord">∥</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.864108em;"><span class="" style="top: -3.113em; margin-right: 0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight">2</span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.222222em;"></span><span class="mbin">+</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.222222em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal">λ</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.336108em;"><span class="" style="top: -2.55em; margin-left: 0em; margin-right: 0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight"><span class="mord mtight"><span class="mord mathrm mtight">wd</span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.15em;"><span class=""></span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mord">∥</span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.05278em;">β</span><span class="mord"><span class="mord">∥</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.864108em;"><span class="" style="top: -3.113em; margin-right: 0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight">2</span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mclose delimcenter" style="top: 0em;"><span class="delimsizing size1">)</span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></p>
<p>Unlike ordinary least squares,</p>
<p>Ridge deliberately penalizes large coefficients.</p>
<p>This penalty improves stability,</p>
<p>but it introduces systematic error.</p>
<p>The estimator is therefore <strong>biased</strong>.</p>
<p>That makes Ridge the ideal place to study how latent geometry influences statistical bias.</p>
<p>Later,</p>
<p>the notes temporarily remove the regularization</p>
<p><span class="katex--display"><span class="katex-display"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="block"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>λ</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">w</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">d</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo separator="true">,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">
\lambda_{\mathrm{wd}}=0,
</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.84444em; vertical-align: -0.15em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal">λ</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.336108em;"><span class="" style="top: -2.55em; margin-left: 0em; margin-right: 0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight"><span class="mord mtight"><span class="mord mathrm mtight">wd</span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.15em;"><span class=""></span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.277778em;"></span><span class="mrel">=</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.277778em;"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.83888em; vertical-align: -0.19444em;"></span><span class="mord">0</span><span class="mpunct">,</span></span></span></span></span></span></p>
<p>reducing Ridge to Ordinary Least Squares.</p>
<p>OLS has zero bias,</p>
<p>allowing us to isolate and study variance separately.</p>
<p>The two lemmas therefore investigate complementary questions.</p>
<p><strong>Lemma 1</strong></p>
<blockquote>
<p>How does anisotropy change the bias introduced by regularization?</p>
</blockquote>
<p><strong>Lemma 2</strong></p>
<blockquote>
<p>If regularization is removed entirely, how does anisotropy affect estimator variance?</p>
</blockquote>
<p>Together,</p>
<p>these two results characterize the two fundamental sources of downstream estimation error.</p>
<hr>
<h1 id="why-we-consider-the-worst-case-downstream-task">Why We Consider The Worst-Case Downstream Task</h1>
<p>One subtle but extremely important point is the phrase</p>
<blockquote>
<p>“an adversarial downstream task.”</p>
</blockquote>
<p>This does <strong>not</strong> mean an attacker is modifying the data.</p>
<p>Instead,</p>
<p>remember the philosophy established in Part 10.</p>
<p>The encoder does not know which downstream task will eventually appear.</p>
<p>Some future task may happen to rely heavily on a semantic feature that the encoder placed into one of its narrowest latent directions.</p>
<p>If that happens,</p>
<p>the downstream learner is immediately at a disadvantage.</p>
<p>To guarantee good performance <strong>for every possible future task</strong>, we must analyze the worst alignment that could occur.</p>
<p>Mathematically,</p>
<p>this worst case happens when the true parameter vector</p>
<p><span class="katex--display"><span class="katex-display"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="block"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>β</mi><mtext>true</mtext></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">
\beta_{\text{true}}
</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.88888em; vertical-align: -0.19444em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.05278em;">β</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.280556em;"><span class="" style="top: -2.55em; margin-left: -0.05278em; margin-right: 0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight"><span class="mord text mtight"><span class="mord mtight">true</span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.15em;"><span class=""></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></p>
<p>aligns perfectly with the eigenvector corresponding to the smallest eigenvalue.</p>
<p>Intuitively,</p>
<p>the downstream task asks the model to make predictions using the weakest, narrowest, least informative direction in the entire representation.</p>
<p>If the representation performs well even under this worst possible alignment,</p>
<p>it will necessarily perform at least as well for all easier alignments.</p>
<p>This minimax viewpoint is why the proof focuses on the smallest eigenvalue rather than the average one.</p>
<p>The next lemma now becomes much easier to understand.</p>
<p>It asks a very natural question:</p>
<blockquote>
<p><strong>If the downstream task depends mostly on the weakest direction of the embedding space, how much extra bias does Ridge regularization introduce?</strong></p>
</blockquote>
<h1 id="lemma-1-—-why-anisotropy-increases-ridge-bias">Lemma 1 — Why Anisotropy Increases Ridge Bias</h1>
<p>We now analyze the first source of estimation error: <strong>bias</strong>.</p>
<p>Recall that Ridge regression solves</p>
<p><span class="katex--display"><span class="katex-display"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="block"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>β</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>=</mo><mi>arg</mi><mo>⁡</mo><munder><mrow><mi>min</mi><mo>⁡</mo></mrow><mi>β</mi></munder><mrow><mo fence="true">(</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∥</mi><mi>y</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>Z</mi><mi>β</mi><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">∥</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>λ</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">w</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">d</mi></mrow></msub><mi mathvariant="normal">∥</mi><mi>β</mi><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">∥</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo fence="true">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\beta} = \arg\min_{\beta} \left( \|y - Z\beta\|^2 + \lambda_{\mathrm{wd}}\|\beta\|^2 \right)</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 1.15232em; vertical-align: -0.19444em;"></span><span class="mord accent"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.95788em;"><span class="" style="top: -3em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 3em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.05278em;">β</span></span><span class="" style="top: -3.26344em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 3em;"></span><span class="accent-body" style="left: -0.16666em;"><span class="mord">^</span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.19444em;"><span class=""></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.277778em;"></span><span class="mrel">=</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.277778em;"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 1.75232em; vertical-align: -0.888216em;"></span><span class="mop">ar<span style="margin-right: 0.01389em;">g</span></span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.166667em;"></span><span class="mop op-limits"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.66786em;"><span class="" style="top: -2.34789em; margin-left: 0em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 3em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight"><span class="mord mathnormal mtight" style="margin-right: 0.05278em;">β</span></span></span></span><span class="" style="top: -3em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 3em;"></span><span class=""><span class="mop">min</span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.888216em;"><span class=""></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.166667em;"></span><span class="minner"><span class="mopen delimcenter" style="top: 0em;"><span class="delimsizing size1">(</span></span><span class="mord">∥</span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.03588em;">y</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.222222em;"></span><span class="mbin">−</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.222222em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.05278em;">Zβ</span><span class="mord"><span class="mord">∥</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.864108em;"><span class="" style="top: -3.113em; margin-right: 0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight">2</span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.222222em;"></span><span class="mbin">+</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.222222em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal">λ</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.336108em;"><span class="" style="top: -2.55em; margin-left: 0em; margin-right: 0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight"><span class="mord mtight"><span class="mord mathrm mtight">wd</span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.15em;"><span class=""></span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mord">∥</span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.05278em;">β</span><span class="mord"><span class="mord">∥</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.864108em;"><span class="" style="top: -3.113em; margin-right: 0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight">2</span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mclose delimcenter" style="top: 0em;"><span class="delimsizing size1">)</span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></p>
<p>Unlike Ordinary Least Squares, Ridge intentionally sacrifices perfect accuracy on the training data in exchange for a more stable solution.</p>
<p>It does this by shrinking the learned coefficients toward zero.</p>
<p>This phenomenon is called <strong>shrinkage</strong>.</p>
<hr>
<h1 id="where-does-the-bias-come-from">Where Does The Bias Come From?</h1>
<p>Suppose the true relationship between the embeddings and labels is</p>
<p><span class="katex--display"><span class="katex-display"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="block"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>Z</mi><msub><mi>β</mi><mtext>true</mtext></msub><mo>+</mo><mi>ε</mi><mo separator="true">,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">
y=Z\beta_{\text{true}}+\varepsilon,
</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.625em; vertical-align: -0.19444em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.03588em;">y</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.277778em;"></span><span class="mrel">=</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.277778em;"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.88888em; vertical-align: -0.19444em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.07153em;">Z</span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.05278em;">β</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.280556em;"><span class="" style="top: -2.55em; margin-left: -0.05278em; margin-right: 0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight"><span class="mord text mtight"><span class="mord mtight">true</span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.15em;"><span class=""></span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.222222em;"></span><span class="mbin">+</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.222222em;"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.625em; vertical-align: -0.19444em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal">ε</span><span class="mpunct">,</span></span></span></span></span></span></p>
<p>where</p>
<ul>
<li><span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>β</mi><mtext>true</mtext></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta_{\text{true}}</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.88888em; vertical-align: -0.19444em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.05278em;">β</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.280556em;"><span class="" style="top: -2.55em; margin-left: -0.05278em; margin-right: 0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight"><span class="mord text mtight"><span class="mord mtight">true</span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.15em;"><span class=""></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span> is the unknown true parameter vector,</li>
<li><span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>ε</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\varepsilon</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.43056em; vertical-align: 0em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal">ε</span></span></span></span></span> is random observation noise.</li>
</ul>
<p>If we had infinitely many samples and used Ordinary Least Squares, the expected estimator would recover</p>
<p><span class="katex--display"><span class="katex-display"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="block"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>β</mi><mtext>true</mtext></msub><mi mathvariant="normal">.</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">
\beta_{\text{true}}.
</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.88888em; vertical-align: -0.19444em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.05278em;">β</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.280556em;"><span class="" style="top: -2.55em; margin-left: -0.05278em; margin-right: 0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight"><span class="mord text mtight"><span class="mord mtight">true</span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.15em;"><span class=""></span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mord">.</span></span></span></span></span></span></p>
<p>Ridge deliberately refuses to do this.</p>
<p>Instead,</p>
<p>every coefficient is pulled closer to zero.</p>
<p>Therefore,</p>
<p>even with infinite data,</p>
<p><span class="katex--display"><span class="katex-display"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="block"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="double-struck">E</mi><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>β</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo stretchy="false">]</mo><mo mathvariant="normal">≠</mo><msub><mi>β</mi><mtext>true</mtext></msub><mi mathvariant="normal">.</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">
\mathbb E[\hat\beta]
\neq
\beta_{\text{true}}.
</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 1.20788em; vertical-align: -0.25em;"></span><span class="mord mathbb">E</span><span class="mopen">[</span><span class="mord accent"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.95788em;"><span class="" style="top: -3em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 3em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.05278em;">β</span></span><span class="" style="top: -3.26344em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 3em;"></span><span class="accent-body" style="left: -0.16666em;"><span class="mord">^</span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.19444em;"><span class=""></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mclose">]</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.277778em;"></span><span class="mrel"><span class="mrel"><span class="mord vbox"><span class="thinbox"><span class="rlap"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.88888em; vertical-align: -0.19444em;"></span><span class="inner"><span class="mord"><span class="mrel"></span></span></span><span class="fix"></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mrel">=</span></span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.277778em;"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.88888em; vertical-align: -0.19444em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.05278em;">β</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.280556em;"><span class="" style="top: -2.55em; margin-left: -0.05278em; margin-right: 0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight"><span class="mord text mtight"><span class="mord mtight">true</span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.15em;"><span class=""></span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mord">.</span></span></span></span></span></span></p>
<p>The estimator has become biased.</p>
<p>The mathematical expression for this bias is</p>
<p><span class="katex--display"><span class="katex-display"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="block"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Bias</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>β</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>λ</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">w</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">d</mi></mrow></msub><msup><mrow><mo fence="true">(</mo><msup><mi>Z</mi><mi>T</mi></msup><mi>Z</mi><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>λ</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">w</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">d</mi></mrow></msub><mi>I</mi><mo fence="true">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><msub><mi>β</mi><mtext>true</mtext></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\operatorname{Bias}(\hat{\beta}) = -\lambda_{\mathrm{wd}} \left( Z^T Z + \lambda_{\mathrm{wd}} I \right)^{-1} \beta_{\text{true}}</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 1.20788em; vertical-align: -0.25em;"></span><span class="mop"><span class="mord mathrm">Bias</span></span><span class="mopen">(</span><span class="mord accent"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.95788em;"><span class="" style="top: -3em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 3em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.05278em;">β</span></span><span class="" style="top: -3.26344em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 3em;"></span><span class="accent-body" style="left: -0.16666em;"><span class="mord">^</span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.19444em;"><span class=""></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mclose">)</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.277778em;"></span><span class="mrel">=</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.277778em;"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 1.44535em; vertical-align: -0.35001em;"></span><span class="mord">−</span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal">λ</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.336108em;"><span class="" style="top: -2.55em; margin-left: 0em; margin-right: 0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight"><span class="mord mtight"><span class="mord mathrm mtight">wd</span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.15em;"><span class=""></span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.166667em;"></span><span class="minner"><span class="minner"><span class="mopen delimcenter" style="top: 0em;"><span class="delimsizing size1">(</span></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.07153em;">Z</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.891331em;"><span class="" style="top: -3.113em; margin-right: 0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mathnormal mtight" style="margin-right: 0.13889em;">T</span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.07153em;">Z</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.222222em;"></span><span class="mbin">+</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.222222em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal">λ</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.336108em;"><span class="" style="top: -2.55em; margin-left: 0em; margin-right: 0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight"><span class="mord mtight"><span class="mord mathrm mtight">wd</span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.15em;"><span class=""></span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.07847em;">I</span><span class="mclose delimcenter" style="top: 0em;"><span class="delimsizing size1">)</span></span></span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 1.09534em;"><span class="" style="top: -3.34423em; margin-right: 0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight"><span class="mord mtight">−</span><span class="mord mtight">1</span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.166667em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.05278em;">β</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.280556em;"><span class="" style="top: -2.55em; margin-left: -0.05278em; margin-right: 0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight"><span class="mord text mtight"><span class="mord mtight">true</span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.15em;"><span class=""></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></p>
<p>Although this expression initially appears intimidating,</p>
<p>it contains a very intuitive idea.</p>
<p>The inverse matrix</p>
<p><span class="katex--display"><span class="katex-display"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="block"><semantics><mrow><msup><mrow><mo fence="true">(</mo><msup><mi>Z</mi><mi>T</mi></msup><mi>Z</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>λ</mi><mi>I</mi><mo fence="true">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">
\left(
Z^TZ+\lambda I
\right)^{-1}
</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 1.44535em; vertical-align: -0.35001em;"></span><span class="minner"><span class="minner"><span class="mopen delimcenter" style="top: 0em;"><span class="delimsizing size1">(</span></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.07153em;">Z</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.891331em;"><span class="" style="top: -3.113em; margin-right: 0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mathnormal mtight" style="margin-right: 0.13889em;">T</span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.07153em;">Z</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.222222em;"></span><span class="mbin">+</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.222222em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal">λ</span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.07847em;">I</span><span class="mclose delimcenter" style="top: 0em;"><span class="delimsizing size1">)</span></span></span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 1.09534em;"><span class="" style="top: -3.34423em; margin-right: 0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight"><span class="mord mtight">−</span><span class="mord mtight">1</span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></p>
<p>determines <strong>how much each latent direction is shrunk</strong>.</p>
<p>The amount of shrinkage depends entirely on the eigenvalues of the covariance matrix.</p>
<p>Thus,</p>
<p>the geometry of the representation directly controls the amount of statistical bias.</p>
<hr>
<h1 id="looking-at-one-eigen-direction-at-a-time">Looking At One Eigen-Direction At A Time</h1>
<p>The covariance matrix can always be decomposed into independent principal directions.</p>
<p>Instead of thinking about all dimensions simultaneously,</p>
<p>imagine analyzing only one eigenvector.</p>
<p>Along one eigen-direction,</p>
<p>the matrix behaves like the scalar</p>
<p><span class="katex--display"><span class="katex-display"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="block"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>λ</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mi mathvariant="normal">.</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">
\lambda_k.
</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.84444em; vertical-align: -0.15em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal">λ</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.336108em;"><span class="" style="top: -2.55em; margin-left: 0em; margin-right: 0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mathnormal mtight" style="margin-right: 0.03148em;">k</span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.15em;"><span class=""></span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mord">.</span></span></span></span></span></span></p>
<p>The bias contribution in that direction becomes</p>
<p><span class="katex--display"><span class="katex-display"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="block"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><msub><mi>λ</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">w</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">d</mi></mrow></msub><mrow><msub><mi>λ</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>λ</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">w</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">d</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></mfrac><mi mathvariant="normal">.</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">
\frac{\lambda_{\mathrm{wd}}}
{\lambda_k+\lambda_{\mathrm{wd}}}.
</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 2.20744em; vertical-align: -0.836em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mopen nulldelimiter"></span><span class="mfrac"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 1.37144em;"><span class="" style="top: -2.314em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 3em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal">λ</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.336108em;"><span class="" style="top: -2.55em; margin-left: 0em; margin-right: 0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mathnormal mtight" style="margin-right: 0.03148em;">k</span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.15em;"><span class=""></span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.222222em;"></span><span class="mbin">+</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.222222em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal">λ</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.336108em;"><span class="" style="top: -2.55em; margin-left: 0em; margin-right: 0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight"><span class="mord mtight"><span class="mord mathrm mtight">wd</span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.15em;"><span class=""></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="" style="top: -3.23em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 3em;"></span><span class="frac-line" style="border-bottom-width: 0.04em;"></span></span><span class="" style="top: -3.677em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 3em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal">λ</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.336108em;"><span class="" style="top: -2.55em; margin-left: 0em; margin-right: 0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight"><span class="mord mtight"><span class="mord mathrm mtight">wd</span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.15em;"><span class=""></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.836em;"><span class=""></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mclose nulldelimiter"></span></span><span class="mord">.</span></span></span></span></span></span></p>
<p>This simple expression explains the entire lemma.</p>
<p>There are only two possibilities.</p>
<p>If</p>
<p><span class="katex--display"><span class="katex-display"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="block"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>λ</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">
\lambda_k
</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.84444em; vertical-align: -0.15em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal">λ</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.336108em;"><span class="" style="top: -2.55em; margin-left: 0em; margin-right: 0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mathnormal mtight" style="margin-right: 0.03148em;">k</span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.15em;"><span class=""></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></p>
<p>is very large,</p>
<p>then</p>
<p><span class="katex--display"><span class="katex-display"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="block"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>λ</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>λ</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">w</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">d</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">
\lambda_k+\lambda_{\mathrm{wd}}
</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.84444em; vertical-align: -0.15em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal">λ</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.336108em;"><span class="" style="top: -2.55em; margin-left: 0em; margin-right: 0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mathnormal mtight" style="margin-right: 0.03148em;">k</span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.15em;"><span class=""></span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.222222em;"></span><span class="mbin">+</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.222222em;"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.84444em; vertical-align: -0.15em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal">λ</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.336108em;"><span class="" style="top: -2.55em; margin-left: 0em; margin-right: 0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight"><span class="mord mtight"><span class="mord mathrm mtight">wd</span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.15em;"><span class=""></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></p>
<p>is also large,</p>
<p>making the fraction small.</p>
<p>Very little shrinkage occurs.</p>
<p>Very little bias is introduced.</p>
<p>However,</p>
<p>if</p>
<p><span class="katex--display"><span class="katex-display"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="block"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>λ</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">
\lambda_k
</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.84444em; vertical-align: -0.15em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal">λ</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.336108em;"><span class="" style="top: -2.55em; margin-left: 0em; margin-right: 0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mathnormal mtight" style="margin-right: 0.03148em;">k</span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.15em;"><span class=""></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></p>
<p>is tiny,</p>
<p>then the denominator becomes much smaller,</p>
<p>causing the fraction to become much larger.</p>
<p>The coefficients along that direction are pulled strongly toward zero.</p>
<p>The statistical bias increases dramatically.</p>
<hr>
<h1 id="why-small-eigenvalues-hurt">Why Small Eigenvalues Hurt</h1>
<p>Imagine trying to estimate a straight line from noisy data.</p>
<p>If the data spans a wide range of <span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.43056em; vertical-align: 0em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal">x</span></span></span></span></span> values,</p>
<p>the slope can be estimated confidently.</p>
<p>Small changes in the observations barely affect the estimate.</p>
<p>Now imagine that all the <span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.43056em; vertical-align: 0em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal">x</span></span></span></span></span> values are almost identical.</p>
<p>The data provides almost no information about the slope.</p>
<p>The estimator cannot distinguish many different possible solutions.</p>
<p>Ridge therefore concludes</p>
<blockquote>
<p>“I do not trust this direction.”</p>
</blockquote>
<p>and shrinks the corresponding coefficient toward zero.</p>
<p>Exactly the same phenomenon occurs inside latent space.</p>
<p>A small eigenvalue means</p>
<p>the data barely varies along that direction.</p>
<p>Since there is little evidence,</p>
<p>Ridge heavily regularizes that coefficient.</p>
<p>The consequence is increased bias.</p>
<hr>
<h1 id="why-the-worst-case-uses-the-smallest-eigenvalue">Why The Worst Case Uses The Smallest Eigenvalue</h1>
<p>The proof now introduces the worst-case downstream task.</p>
<p>Recall that every downstream task corresponds to some unknown parameter vector</p>
<p><span class="katex--display"><span class="katex-display"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="block"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>β</mi><mtext>true</mtext></msub><mi mathvariant="normal">.</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">
\beta_{\text{true}}.
</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.88888em; vertical-align: -0.19444em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.05278em;">β</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.280556em;"><span class="" style="top: -2.55em; margin-left: -0.05278em; margin-right: 0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight"><span class="mord text mtight"><span class="mord mtight">true</span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.15em;"><span class=""></span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mord">.</span></span></span></span></span></span></p>
<p>Different tasks depend on different semantic directions.</p>
<p>Some tasks may primarily use the first principal direction.</p>
<p>Others may depend on the fifth.</p>
<p>Others may require a mixture of many directions.</p>
<p>Since the encoder has no idea which task will eventually appear,</p>
<p>we ask</p>
<blockquote>
<p>Which task would expose the greatest weakness of this representation?</p>
</blockquote>
<p>The answer is straightforward.</p>
<p>The most difficult task is one whose signal lies almost entirely in the weakest direction of the embedding space.</p>
<p>That weakest direction is precisely the eigenvector associated with</p>
<p><span class="katex--display"><span class="katex-display"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="block"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>λ</mi><mi>K</mi></msub><mo separator="true">,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">
\lambda_K,
</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.88888em; vertical-align: -0.19444em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal">λ</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.328331em;"><span class="" style="top: -2.55em; margin-left: 0em; margin-right: 0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mathnormal mtight" style="margin-right: 0.07153em;">K</span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.15em;"><span class=""></span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mpunct">,</span></span></span></span></span></span></p>
<p>the smallest eigenvalue.</p>
<p>If</p>
<p><span class="katex--display"><span class="katex-display"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="block"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>β</mi><mtext>true</mtext></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">
\beta_{\text{true}}
</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.88888em; vertical-align: -0.19444em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.05278em;">β</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.280556em;"><span class="" style="top: -2.55em; margin-left: -0.05278em; margin-right: 0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight"><span class="mord text mtight"><span class="mord mtight">true</span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.15em;"><span class=""></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></p>
<p>points exactly in that direction,</p>
<p>every prediction must rely on the direction suffering the greatest regularization shrinkage.</p>
<p>This creates the largest possible bias.</p>
<hr>
<h1 id="understanding-the-bias-formula">Understanding The Bias Formula</h1>
<p>The notes therefore write</p>
<p><span class="katex--display"><span class="katex-display"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="block"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">∣</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">Bias</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>β</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">∣</mi><mtext>aniso</mtext></msub><mo>≈</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∣</mi><msub><mi>β</mi><mtext>true</mtext></msub><mi mathvariant="normal">∣</mi><mfrac><msub><mi>λ</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">w</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">d</mi></mrow></msub><mrow><msub><mi>λ</mi><mi>K</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>λ</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">w</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">d</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">|\operatorname{Bias}(\hat{\beta})|_{\text{aniso}} \approx |\beta_{\text{true}}| \frac{\lambda_{\mathrm{wd}}}{\lambda_K + \lambda_{\mathrm{wd}}}</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 1.20788em; vertical-align: -0.25em;"></span><span class="mord">∣</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.166667em;"></span><span class="mop"><span class="mord mathrm">Bias</span></span><span class="mopen">(</span><span class="mord accent"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.95788em;"><span class="" style="top: -3em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 3em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.05278em;">β</span></span><span class="" style="top: -3.26344em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 3em;"></span><span class="accent-body" style="left: -0.16666em;"><span class="mord">^</span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.19444em;"><span class=""></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mclose">)</span><span class="mord"><span class="mord">∣</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.317502em;"><span class="" style="top: -2.55em; margin-left: 0em; margin-right: 0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight"><span class="mord text mtight"><span class="mord mtight">aniso</span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.15em;"><span class=""></span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.277778em;"></span><span class="mrel">≈</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.277778em;"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 2.20744em; vertical-align: -0.836em;"></span><span class="mord">∣</span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.05278em;">β</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.280556em;"><span class="" style="top: -2.55em; margin-left: -0.05278em; margin-right: 0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight"><span class="mord text mtight"><span class="mord mtight">true</span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.15em;"><span class=""></span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mord">∣</span><span class="mord"><span class="mopen nulldelimiter"></span><span class="mfrac"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 1.37144em;"><span class="" style="top: -2.314em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 3em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal">λ</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.328331em;"><span class="" style="top: -2.55em; margin-left: 0em; margin-right: 0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mathnormal mtight" style="margin-right: 0.07153em;">K</span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.15em;"><span class=""></span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.222222em;"></span><span class="mbin">+</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.222222em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal">λ</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.336108em;"><span class="" style="top: -2.55em; margin-left: 0em; margin-right: 0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight"><span class="mord mtight"><span class="mord mathrm mtight">wd</span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.15em;"><span class=""></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="" style="top: -3.23em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 3em;"></span><span class="frac-line" style="border-bottom-width: 0.04em;"></span></span><span class="" style="top: -3.677em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 3em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal">λ</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.336108em;"><span class="" style="top: -2.55em; margin-left: 0em; margin-right: 0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight"><span class="mord mtight"><span class="mord mathrm mtight">wd</span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.15em;"><span class=""></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.836em;"><span class=""></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mclose nulldelimiter"></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></p>
<p>Notice that only one quantity depends on the embedding geometry:</p>
<p><span class="katex--display"><span class="katex-display"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="block"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>λ</mi><mi>K</mi></msub><mi mathvariant="normal">.</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">
\lambda_K.
</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.84444em; vertical-align: -0.15em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal">λ</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.328331em;"><span class="" style="top: -2.55em; margin-left: 0em; margin-right: 0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mathnormal mtight" style="margin-right: 0.07153em;">K</span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.15em;"><span class=""></span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mord">.</span></span></span></span></span></span></p>
<p>Everything else is fixed.</p>
<p>Now compare this with the isotropic representation.</p>
<p>In an isotropic embedding,</p>
<p>every eigenvalue equals the average</p>
<p><span class="katex--display"><span class="katex-display"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="block"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>λ</mi><mo>ˉ</mo></mover><mi mathvariant="normal">.</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">
\bar\lambda.
</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.83122em; vertical-align: 0em;"></span><span class="mord accent"><span class="vlist-t"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.83122em;"><span class="" style="top: -3em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 3em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal">λ</span></span><span class="" style="top: -3.26344em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 3em;"></span><span class="accent-body" style="left: -0.25em;"><span class="mord">ˉ</span></span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mord">.</span></span></span></span></span></span></p>
<p>Therefore the corresponding bias becomes</p>
<p><span class="katex--display"><span class="katex-display"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="block"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">∣</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">Bias</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>β</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">∣</mi><mtext>iso</mtext></msub><mo>≈</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∣</mi><msub><mi>β</mi><mtext>true</mtext></msub><mi mathvariant="normal">∣</mi><mfrac><msub><mi>λ</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">w</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">d</mi></mrow></msub><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>λ</mi><mo>ˉ</mo></mover><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>λ</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">w</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">d</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">|\operatorname{Bias}(\hat{\beta})|_{\text{iso}} \approx |\beta_{\text{true}}| \frac{\lambda_{\mathrm{wd}}}{\bar{\lambda} + \lambda_{\mathrm{wd}}}</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 1.20788em; <p>Since anisotropy means</p>
<p><span class="katex--display"><span class="katex-display"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="block"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>λ</mi><mi>K</mi></msub><mo>&lt;</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>λ</mi><mo>ˉ</mo></mover><mo separator="true">,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">
\lambda_K
&lt;
\bar\lambda,

<p>we have</p>

\lambda_K+\lambda_{\mathrm{wd}}

<p>Thus,</p>
