vertical-align: -0.25em;"></span><span class="mord">∣</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.166667em;"></span><span class="mop"><span class="mord mathrm">Bias</span></span><span class="mopen">(</span><span class="mord accent"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.95788em;"><span class="" style="top: -3em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 3em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.05278em;">β</span></span><span class="" style="top: -3.26344em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 3em;"></span><span class="accent-body" style="left: -0.16666em;"><span class="mord">^</span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.19444em;"><span class=""></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mclose">)</span><span class="mord"><span class="mord">∣</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.317502em;"><span class="" style="top: -2.55em; margin-left: 0em; margin-right: 0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight"><span class="mord text mtight"><span class="mord mtight">aniso</span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.15em;"><span class=""></span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.277778em;"></span><span class="mrel">≈</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.277778em;"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 1.20788em; vertical-align: -0.25em;"></span><span class="mord">∣</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.166667em;"></span><span class="mop"><span class="mord mathrm">Bias</span></span><span class="mopen">(</span><span class="mord accent"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.95788em;"><span class="" style="top: -3em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 3em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.05278em;">β</span></span><span class="" style="top: -3.26344em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 3em;"></span><span class="accent-body" style="left: -0.16666em;"><span class="mord">^</span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.19444em;"><span class=""></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mclose">)</span><span class="mord"><span class="mord">∣</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.317502em;"><span class="" style="top: -2.55em; margin-left: 0em; margin-right: 0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight"><span class="mord text mtight"><span class="mord mtight">iso</span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.15em;"><span class=""></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></p>
<p>Nothing mysterious has happened.</p>
<p>The entire proof reduces to one intuitive fact:</p>
<blockquote>
<p><strong>Ridge trusts directions with abundant variance and distrusts directions with little variance.</strong></p>
</blockquote>
<p>An anisotropic embedding inevitably contains weak directions.</p>
<p>Therefore it inevitably creates larger worst-case bias.</p>
<hr>
<h1 id="lemma-2-—-why-the-proof-switches-to-ordinary-least-squares">Lemma 2 — Why The Proof Switches To Ordinary Least Squares</h1>
<p>The next lemma studies <strong>variance</strong> instead of bias.</p>
<p>However,</p>
<p>Ridge already possesses bias by construction.</p>
<p>If we continued using Ridge,</p>
<p>its variance analysis would become mixed together with the effects of regularization.</p>
<p>To isolate variance alone,</p>
<p>the proof temporarily removes regularization,</p>
<p>setting</p>
<p><span class="katex--display"><span class="katex-display"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="block"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>λ</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">w</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">d</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0.</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">
\lambda_{\mathrm{wd}}=0.
</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.84444em; vertical-align: -0.15em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal">λ</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.336108em;"><span class="" style="top: -2.55em; margin-left: 0em; margin-right: 0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight"><span class="mord mtight"><span class="mord mathrm mtight">wd</span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.15em;"><span class=""></span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.277778em;"></span><span class="mrel">=</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.277778em;"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.64444em; vertical-align: 0em;"></span><span class="mord">0.</span></span></span></span></span></span></p>
<p>Ridge now becomes Ordinary Least Squares (OLS).</p>
<p>OLS has an important property.</p>
<p>Assuming the standard linear model assumptions hold,</p>
<p><span class="katex--display"><span class="katex-display"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="block"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="double-struck">E</mi><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>β</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo stretchy="false">]</mo><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>β</mi><mtext>true</mtext></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{E}[\hat{\beta}] = \beta_{\text{true}}</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 1.20788em; vertical-align: -0.25em;"></span><span class="mord mathbb">E</span><span class="mopen">[</span><span class="mord accent"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.95788em;"><span class="" style="top: -3em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 3em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.05278em;">β</span></span><span class="" style="top: -3.26344em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 3em;"></span><span class="accent-body" style="left: -0.16666em;"><span class="mord">^</span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.19444em;"><span class=""></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mclose">]</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.277778em;"></span><span class="mrel">=</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.277778em;"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.88888em; vertical-align: -0.19444em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.05278em;">β</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.280556em;"><span class="" style="top: -2.55em; margin-left: -0.05278em; margin-right: 0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight"><span class="mord text mtight"><span class="mord mtight">true</span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.15em;"><span class=""></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></p>
<p>Its bias is exactly zero.</p>
<p>Now every remaining source of estimation error comes purely from variance.</p>
<hr>
<h1 id="where-does-the-variance-formula-come-from">Where Does The Variance Formula Come From?</h1>
<p>Suppose we repeatedly collect many different training datasets from the same population.</p>
<p>Each dataset contains slightly different samples.</p>
<p>Training OLS on every dataset will produce slightly different parameter vectors</p>
<p><span class="katex--display"><span class="katex-display"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="block"><semantics><mrow><msup><mover accent="true"><mi>β</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo separator="true">,</mo><msup><mover accent="true"><mi>β</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo separator="true">,</mo><msup><mover accent="true"><mi>β</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo separator="true">,</mo><mo>…</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">
\hat\beta^{(1)},
\hat\beta^{(2)},
\hat\beta^{(3)},\ldots
</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 1.15232em; vertical-align: -0.19444em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord accent"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.95788em;"><span class="" style="top: -3em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 3em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.05278em;">β</span></span><span class="" style="top: -3.26344em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 3em;"></span><span class="accent-body" style="left: -0.16666em;"><span class="mord">^</span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.19444em;"><span class=""></span></span></span></span></span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.938em;"><span class="" style="top: -3.113em; margin-right: 0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight"><span class="mopen mtight">(</span><span class="mord mtight">1</span><span class="mclose mtight">)</span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mpunct">,</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.166667em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord accent"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.95788em;"><span class="" style="top: -3em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 3em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.05278em;">β</span></span><span class="" style="top: -3.26344em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 3em;"></span><span class="accent-body" style="left: -0.16666em;"><span class="mord">^</span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.19444em;"><span class=""></span></span></span></span></span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.938em;"><span class="" style="top: -3.113em; margin-right: 0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight"><span class="mopen mtight">(</span><span class="mord mtight">2</span><span class="mclose mtight">)</span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mpunct">,</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.166667em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord accent"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.95788em;"><span class="" style="top: -3em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 3em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.05278em;">β</span></span><span class="" style="top: -3.26344em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 3em;"></span><span class="accent-body" style="left: -0.16666em;"><span class="mord">^</span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.19444em;"><span class=""></span></span></span></span></span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.938em;"><span class="" style="top: -3.113em; margin-right: 0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight"><span class="mopen mtight">(</span><span class="mord mtight">3</span><span class="mclose mtight">)</span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mpunct">,</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.166667em;"></span><span class="minner">…</span></span></span></span></span></span></p>
<p>Variance measures how much these estimated parameters fluctuate.</p>
<p>Under the classical linear regression assumptions,</p>
<p>the covariance matrix of the estimator is</p>
<p><span class="katex--display"><span class="katex-display"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="block"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Var</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>β</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>σ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>Z</mi><mi>T</mi></msup><mi>Z</mi><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\operatorname{Var}(\hat{\beta}) = \sigma^2 (Z^T Z)^{-1}</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 1.20788em; vertical-align: -0.25em;"></span><span class="mop"><span class="mord mathrm">Var</span></span><span class="mopen">(</span><span class="mord accent"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.95788em;"><span class="" style="top: -3em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 3em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.05278em;">β</span></span><span class="" style="top: -3.26344em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 3em;"></span><span class="accent-body" style="left: -0.16666em;"><span class="mord">^</span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.19444em;"><span class=""></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mclose">)</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.277778em;"></span><span class="mrel">=</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.277778em;"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 1.14133em; vertical-align: -0.25em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.03588em;">σ</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.864108em;"><span class="" style="top: -3.113em; margin-right: 0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight">2</span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mopen">(</span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.07153em;">Z</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.891331em;"><span class="" style="top: -3.113em; margin-right: 0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mathnormal mtight" style="margin-right: 0.13889em;">T</span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.07153em;">Z</span><span class="mclose"><span class="mclose">)</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.864108em;"><span class="" style="top: -3.113em; margin-right: 0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight"><span class="mord mtight">−</span><span class="mord mtight">1</span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></p>
<p>where</p>
<p><span class="katex--display"><span class="katex-display"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="block"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>σ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">
\sigma^2
</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.864108em; vertical-align: 0em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.03588em;">σ</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.864108em;"><span class="" style="top: -3.113em; margin-right: 0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight">2</span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></p>
<p>is the variance of the observation noise.</p>
<p>Immediately,</p>
<p>the geometry appears again.</p>
<p>The covariance depends on the inverse of</p>
<p><span class="katex--display"><span class="katex-display"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="block"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>Z</mi><mi>T</mi></msup><mi>Z</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">.</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">
Z^TZ.
</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.891331em; vertical-align: 0em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.07153em;">Z</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.891331em;"><span class="" style="top: -3.113em; margin-right: 0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mathnormal mtight" style="margin-right: 0.13889em;">T</span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.07153em;">Z</span><span class="mord">.</span></span></span></span></span></span></p>
<p>Since matrix inversion reciprocates eigenvalues,</p>
<p>each eigenvalue</p>
<p><span class="katex--display"><span class="katex-display"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="block"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>λ</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">
\lambda_k
</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.84444em; vertical-align: -0.15em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal">λ</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.336108em;"><span class="" style="top: -2.55em; margin-left: 0em; margin-right: 0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mathnormal mtight" style="margin-right: 0.03148em;">k</span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.15em;"><span class=""></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></p>
<p>becomes</p>
<p><span class="katex--display"><span class="katex-display"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="block"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><msub><mi>λ</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></mfrac><mi mathvariant="normal">.</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">
\frac1{\lambda_k}.
</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 2.15744em; vertical-align: -0.836em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mopen nulldelimiter"></span><span class="mfrac"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 1.32144em;"><span class="" style="top: -2.314em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 3em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal">λ</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.336108em;"><span class="" style="top: -2.55em; margin-left: 0em; margin-right: 0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mathnormal mtight" style="margin-right: 0.03148em;">k</span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.15em;"><span class=""></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="" style="top: -3.23em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 3em;"></span><span class="frac-line" style="border-bottom-width: 0.04em;"></span></span><span class="" style="top: -3.677em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 3em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord">1</span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.836em;"><span class=""></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mclose nulldelimiter"></span></span><span class="mord">.</span></span></span></span></span></span></p>
<p>This is the key observation of the second lemma.</p>
<p>Large eigenvalues become small inverse values,</p>
<p>contributing little variance.</p>
<p>Small eigenvalues become enormous inverse values,</p>
<p>causing estimator variance to explode.</p>
<hr>
<h1 id="why-the-trace-measures-total-variance">Why The Trace Measures Total Variance</h1>
<p>The covariance matrix contains one variance value for every parameter,</p>
<p>along with their correlations.</p>
<p>To summarize the total uncertainty with a single number,</p>
<p>the proof computes its trace,</p>
<p><span class="katex--display"><span class="katex-display"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="block"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">tr</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo fence="true">(</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Var</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>β</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo fence="true">)</mo></mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">.</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">
\operatorname{tr}
\left(
\operatorname{Var}(\hat\beta)
\right).
</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 1.80002em; vertical-align: -0.65002em;"></span><span class="mop"><span class="mord mathrm">tr</span></span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.166667em;"></span><span class="minner"><span class="mopen delimcenter" style="top: 0em;"><span class="delimsizing size2">(</span></span><span class="mop"><span class="mord mathrm">Var</span></span><span class="mopen">(</span><span class="mord accent"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.95788em;"><span class="" style="top: -3em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 3em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.05278em;">β</span></span><span class="" style="top: -3.26344em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 3em;"></span><span class="accent-body" style="left: -0.16666em;"><span class="mord">^</span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.19444em;"><span class=""></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mclose">)</span><span class="mclose delimcenter" style="top: 0em;"><span class="delimsizing size2">)</span></span></span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.166667em;"></span><span class="mord">.</span></span></span></span></span></span></p>
<p>Since the trace equals the sum of the eigenvalues,</p>
<p>this becomes</p>
<p><span class="katex--display"><span class="katex-display"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="block"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">tr</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Var</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>β</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>σ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><munderover><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>K</mi></munderover><mfrac><mn>1</mn><msub><mi>λ</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\operatorname{tr}(\operatorname{Var}(\hat{\beta})) = \sigma^2 \sum_{k=1}^{K} \frac{1}{\lambda_k}</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 1.20788em; <p>Notice how different this is from total embedding variance.</p>
<p>Earlier,</p>
<p>large eigenvalues were desirable because they represented rich information.</p>
<p>Now,</p>
<p>small eigenvalues become especially dangerous because their reciprocals become very large.</p>
<p>Even a single tiny eigenvalue can dominate the entire sum,</p>
<p>making the estimator extremely unstable.</p>
<hr>
<h1 id="why-isotropy-minimizes-variance">Why Isotropy Minimizes Variance</h1>
<p>Suppose the total variance</p>

\sum_k\lambda_k

<p>is fixed.</p>
<p>There are infinitely many ways to distribute it.</p>
<p>One possibility is</p>
<p><span class="katex--display"><span class="katex-display"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="block"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>5</mn><mo separator="true">,</mo><mn>5</mn><mo separator="true">,</mo><mn>5</mn><mo separator="true">,</mo><mn>5</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">.</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">
(5,5,5,5).

<p>Another is</p>
<p><span class="katex--display"><span class="katex-display"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="block"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>18</mn><mo separator="true">,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo separator="true">,</mo><mn>0.5</mn><mo separator="true">,</mo><mn>0.5</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">.</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">
(18,1,0.5,0.5).
</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 1em; vertical-align: -0.25em;"></span><span class="mopen">(</span><span class="mord">18</span><span class="mpunct">,</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.166667em;"></span><span class="mord">1</span><span class="mpunct">,</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.166667em;"></span><span class="mord">0.5</span><span class="mpunct">,</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.166667em;"></span><span class="mord">0.5</span><span class="mclose">)</span><span class="mord">.</span></span></span></span></span></span></p>
<p>Both have identical total variance.</p>
<p>However,</p>
<p>the second distribution contains extremely small eigenvalues.</p>
<p>Taking reciprocals magnifies these dramatically.</p>
<p>Consequently,</p>
<p><span class="katex--display"><span class="katex-display"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="block"><semantics><mrow><munder><mo>∑</mo><mi>k</mi></munder><mfrac><mn>1</mn><msub><mi>λ</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">
\sum_k\frac1{\lambda_k}

<p>becomes much larger.</p>
<p>The proof formalizes this intuition using Jensen’s Inequality,</p>
<p>showing that whenever the eigenvalues are unequal,</p>
<p><span class="katex--display"><span class="katex-display"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="block"><semantics><mrow><munderover><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>K</mi></munderover><mfrac><mn>1</mn><msub><mi>λ</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></mfrac><mo>≈</mo><mfrac><mi>K</mi><mover accent="true"><mi>λ</mi><mo>ˉ</mo></mover></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sum_{k=1}^{K} \frac{1}{\lambda_k} \approx \frac{K}{\bar{\lambda}}</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 3.13045em; margin-left: 0em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 3.05em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight"><span class="mord mathnormal mtight" style="margin-right: 0.03148em;">k</span><span class="mrel mtight">=</span><span class="mord mtight">1</span></span></span></span><span class="" style="top: -3.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 3.05em;"></span><span class=""><span class="mop op-symbol large-op">∑</span></span></span><span class="" style="top: -4.3em; margin-left: 0em; margin-right: 0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mathnormal mtight" style="margin-right: 0.03148em;">k</span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.15em;"><span class=""></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="" style="top: -3.23em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 3em;"></span><span class="frac-line" style="border-bottom-width: 0.04em;"></span></span><span class="" style="top: -3.677em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 3em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord">1</span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.836em;"><span class=""></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mclose nulldelimiter"></span></span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.277778em;"></span><span class="mrel">≈</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.277778em;"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 2.08155em; vertical-align: -0.72122em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mopen nulldelimiter"></span><span class="mfrac"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 1.36033em;"><span class="" style="top: -2.27878em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 3em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord accent"><span class="vlist-t"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.83122em;"><span class="" style="top: -3em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 3em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal">λ</span></span><span class="" style="top: -3.26344em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 3em;"></span><span class="accent-body" style="left: -0.25em;"><span class="mord">ˉ</span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="" style="top: -3.23em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 3em;"></span><span class="frac-line" style="border-bottom-width: 0.04em;"></span></span><span class="" style="top: -3.677em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 3em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.07153em;">K</span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.72122em;"><span class=""></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mclose nulldelimiter"></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></p>
<p>Equality occurs only when every eigenvalue is identical.</p>
<p>Thus,</p>
<p>among all embeddings with the same total variance,</p>
<p>the isotropic one uniquely minimizes estimator variance.</p>
<hr>
<h1 id="what-has-actually-been-proven">What Has Actually Been Proven</h1>
<p>The two lemmas establish complementary results.</p>
<p><strong>Lemma 1</strong></p>
<p>An anisotropic embedding contains narrow directions.</p>
<p>Ridge shrinks those directions more aggressively.</p>
<p>Therefore the worst-case regularization bias increases.</p>
<p><strong>Lemma 2</strong></p>
<p>An anisotropic embedding also contains small eigenvalues.</p>
<p>OLS variance depends on the inverse eigenvalues.</p>
<p>Therefore the estimator becomes less stable across different training datasets.</p>
<p>Taken together,</p>
<p>the results show that anisotropy simultaneously increases both fundamental components of statistical estimation error under linear regression.</p>
<p>This does <strong>not</strong> prove that isotropy is universally optimal for every possible machine learning algorithm.</p>
<p>Rather,</p>
<p>it proves a much more precise statement:</p>
<blockquote>
<p><strong>Among linear downstream estimators, and under the assumptions of the classical linear regression model, an isotropic covariance spectrum minimizes the worst-case effects of both regularization bias and estimator variance when total variance is held fixed.</strong></p>
</blockquote>
<p>This conclusion forms the bridge into Part 12, where the notes ask an obvious next question:</p>
<blockquote>
<p><strong>If isotropy is optimal for linear probes, does the same conclusion remain true for non-linear estimators?</strong></p>
</blockquote>
<p>Unknown downstream task<br>
↓<br>
Need some downstream learner to analyze<br>
↓<br>
Choose linear probe<br>
↓<br>
Linear probe error = Bias + Variance<br>
↓<br>
Show isotropy minimizes both<br>
↓<br>
Nice result…<br>
BUT<br>
only for linear probes<br>
↓<br>
Need to check nonlinear estimators<br>
↓<br>
Part 12</p>
<h3 id="part-12-non-linear-probing-optimality">Part 12: Non-Linear Probing Optimality</h3>
<p><strong>Beyond the Linear Assumption</strong> While Part 11 proved that anisotropic covariance inflates risk in linear models, modern frozen-encoder evaluations increasingly rely on non-linear probing to capture complex semantic boundaries. To mathematically guarantee that a JEPA foundation model is strictly optimal, we must analyze the worst-case risk across non-linear estimators.</p>
<p>We evaluate the two mathematically tractable non-linear regimes: radius-based <span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.69444em; vertical-align: 0em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.03148em;">k</span></span></span></span></span>-Nearest Neighbors (<span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.69444em; vertical-align: 0em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.03148em;">k</span></span></span></span></span>-NN) and Nadaraya-Watson kernel regression.</p>
<p><strong>1. <p><strong>The Fisher Information Bottleneck</strong> To find the optimal embedding density <span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p(z)</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 1em; vertical-align: -0.25em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal">p</span><span class="mopen">(</span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.04398em;">z</span><span class="mclose">)</span></span></span></span></span>, we must integrate the pointwise bias of these estimators over the entire query distribution to compute the Integrated Squared Bias (ISB).</p>
<p>Mathematical derivation reveals that for both non-linear estimators, the dominant term dictating the error is structurally identical. It depends fundamentally on <span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>J</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">J(p)</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 1em; <p>This establishes a rigorous, absolute mathematical constraint: to minimize the prediction error for any arbitrary non-linear downstream task, the JEPA objective must force the representation density <span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.625em; vertical-align: -0.19444em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal">p</span></span></span></span></span> to minimize its Fisher Information <span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>J</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">J(p)</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 1em; vertical-align: -0.25em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.09618em;">J</span><span class="mopen">(</span><span class="mord mathnormal">p</span><span class="mclose">)</span></span></span></span></span> under a fixed total variance constraint.</p>
<h1 id="part-12-response-1-moving-beyond-linear-probes--estimator-mechanics">Part 12 (Response 1): Moving Beyond Linear Probes &amp; Estimator Mechanics</h1>
<h2 id="i.-the-limitation-of-linear-probing">I. The Limitation of Linear Probing</h2>
<p>Part 11 proved that an anisotropic latent geometry strictly inflates both regularization bias and estimator variance under linear probing (<span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>y</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>=</mo><mi>Z</mi><mi>β</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{y} = Z\beta</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.88888em; vertical-align: -0.19444em;"></span><span class="mord accent"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.69444em;"><span class="" style="top: -3em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 3em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.03588em;">y</span></span><span class="" style="top: -3em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 3em;"></span><span class="accent-body" style="left: -0.19444em;"><span class="mord">^</span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.19444em;"><span class=""></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.277778em;"></span><span class="mrel">=</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.277778em;"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.88888em; vertical-align: -0.19444em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.05278em;">Zβ</span></span></span></span></span>). However, this proof carries an architectural vulnerability: <strong>it assumes a linear decision boundary</strong>.</p>
<p>Real-world semantic decision boundaries (e.g., separating object classes, predicting physical trajectories, or classifying complex sensory states) are almost never hyperplanes. They form complex, non-linear manifolds in latent space.</p>
<p>If an anisotropic representation only fails under linear probes, a downstream practitioner could bypass the problem entirely by replacing the linear probe with a non-linear estimator (e.g., a local neighborhood classifier or a kernel method). If a non-linear probe could extract features equally well from an anisotropic cloud as from an isotropic one, then the argument for forcing isotropic target geometries in JEPAs would collapse.</p>
<p>Part 12 establishes that <strong>anisotropy corrupts local non-linear estimation just as severely as global linear estimation</strong>. To prove this, we must shift from global linear regression to local non-parametric estimators that fit non-linear target functions <span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y(z)</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 1em; vertical-align: -0.25em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.03588em;">y</span><span class="mopen">(</span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.04398em;">z</span><span class="mclose">)</span></span></span></span></span> by sampling local neighborhoods around a query point <span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi mathvariant="double-struck">R</mi><mi>K</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q \in \mathbb{R}^K</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.73354em; vertical-align: -0.19444em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.03588em;">q</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.277778em;"></span><span class="mrel">∈</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.277778em;"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.841331em; vertical-align: 0em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathbb">R</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.841331em;"><span class="" style="top: -3.063em; <h2 id="iii.-estimator-2-nadaraya-watson-kernel-regression">III. Estimator 2: Nadaraya-Watson Kernel Regression</h2>
<p>The hard indicator cutoff of <span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.69444em; vertical-align: 0em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.03148em;">k</span></span></span></span></span>-NN creates discrete step-function predictions as <span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>q</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.625em; vertical-align: -0.19444em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.03588em;">q</span></span></span></span></span> moves through latent space. To model smooth, continuous non-linear boundaries, we examine the Nadaraya-Watson kernel regressor.</p>
<h3 id="the-mathematical-definition-1">The Mathematical Definition</h3>

<h3 id="the-mechanics-of-continuous-distance-weighting">The Mechanics of Continuous Distance Weighting</h3>
<p>Unlike the hard boundary of <span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.69444em; vertical-align: 0em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.03148em;">k</span></span></span></span></span>-NN, the Nadaraya-Watson regressor applies a continuous, decaying weight to every sample in the dataset:</p>
<ol>
<li><strong>Soft Radial Distance Decay:</strong> The weight assigned to target <span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>n</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y_n</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.625em; <h2 id="iv.-hard-spherical-windowing-vs.-continuous-kernel-weighting">IV. Hard Spherical Windowing vs. Continuous Kernel Weighting</h2>
<p>Both non-linear estimators approximate the true unknown downstream target function <span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi mathvariant="double-struck">E</mi><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>Y</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∣</mi><mrow></mrow><mi>Z</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y(q) = \mathbb{E}[Y \vert{} Z = q]</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 1em; </table><h3 id="why-latent-density-pz-controls-non-linear-error">Why Latent Density <span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p(z)</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 1em; vertical-align: -0.25em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal">p</span><span class="mopen">(</span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.04398em;">z</span><span class="mclose">)</span></span></span></span></span> Controls Non-Linear Error</h3>
<p>For both estimators, predicting <span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y(q)</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 1em; vertical-align: -0.25em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.03588em;">y</span><span class="mopen">(</span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.03588em;">q</span><span class="mclose">)</span></span></span></span></span> requires estimating the expected value of <span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y(z)</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 1em; vertical-align: -0.25em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.03588em;">y</span><span class="mopen">(</span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.04398em;">z</span><span class="mclose">)</span></span></span></span></span> over a small region around <span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>q</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.625em; vertical-align: -0.19444em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.03588em;">q</span></span></span></span></span>.</p>
<p>If the latent embedding density <span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p(z)</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 1em; vertical-align: -0.25em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal">p</span><span class="mopen">(</span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.04398em;">z</span><span class="mclose">)</span></span></span></span></span> varies rapidly across this region (i.e., if <span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">∇</mi><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\nabla p(q)</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 1em; vertical-align: -0.25em;"></span><span class="mord">∇</span><span class="mord mathnormal">p</span><span class="mopen">(</span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.03588em;">q</span><span class="mclose">)</span></span></span></span></span> is large or anisotropic), the sampled points inside the neighborhood will <strong>not</strong> be uniformly centered around <span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>q</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.625em; vertical-align: -0.19444em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.03588em;">q</span></span></span></span></span>. They will skew heavily toward the direction of higher density.</p>
<p>This spatial skew introduces systematic estimation error—<strong>pointwise non-linear bias</strong>.</p>
<hr>
<p>In <strong>Response 2</strong>, we will perform the local 2nd-order Taylor series expansion of both the target function <span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y(z)</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 1em; vertical-align: -0.25em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.03588em;">y</span><span class="mopen">(</span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.04398em;">z</span><span class="mclose">)</span></span></span></span></span> and the density <span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p(z)</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 1em; vertical-align: -0.25em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal">p</span><span class="mopen">(</span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.04398em;">z</span><span class="mclose">)</span></span></span></span></span> around <span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>q</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.625em; vertical-align: -0.19444em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.03588em;">q</span></span></span></span></span> to derive the exact formula for this pointwise bias.</p>
<h1 id="part-12-response-2-the-local-taylor-expansion--pointwise-bias">Part 12 (Response 2): The Local Taylor Expansion &amp; Pointwise Bias</h1>
<p>To understand how latent embedding geometry directly influences non-linear estimation error, we must derive the exact expression for the prediction bias at a query point <span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi mathvariant="double-struck">R</mi><mi>K</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q \in \mathbb{R}^K</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.73354em; vertical-align: -0.19444em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.03588em;">q</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.277778em;"></span><span class="mrel">∈</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.277778em;"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.841331em; vertical-align: 0em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathbb">R</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.841331em;"><span class="" style="top: -3.063em; margin-right: 0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mathnormal mtight" style="margin-right: 0.07153em;">K</span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span>.</p>
<p>When evaluating a frozen embedding space, the estimator does not have access to the true target function <span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi mathvariant="double-struck">E</mi><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>Y</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∣</mi><mrow></mrow><mi>Z</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y(z) = \mathbb{E}[Y \vert{} Z = z]</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 1em; vertical-align: -0.25em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.03588em;">y</span><span class="mopen">(</span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.04398em;">z</span><span class="mclose">)</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.277778em;"></span><span class="mrel">=</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.277778em;"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 1em; vertical-align: -0.25em;"></span><span class="mord mathbb">E</span><span class="mopen">[</span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.22222em;">Y</span><span class="mord">∣</span><span class="mord"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.07153em;">Z</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.277778em;"></span><span class="mrel">=</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.277778em;"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 1em; vertical-align: -0.25em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.04398em;">z</span><span class="mclose">]</span></span></span></span></span> directly. Instead, it averages local labels <span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>n</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y_n</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.625em; vertical-align: -0.19444em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.03588em;">y</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.151392em;"><span class="" style="top: -2.55em; margin-left: -0.03588em; margin-right: 0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mathnormal mtight">n</span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.15em;"><span class=""></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span> sampled from the empirical density <span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p(z)</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 1em; vertical-align: -0.25em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal">p</span><span class="mopen">(</span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.04398em;">z</span><span class="mclose">)</span></span></span></span></span> around <span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>q</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.625em; vertical-align: -0.19444em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.03588em;">q</span></span></span></span></span>.</p>
<hr>
<h2 id="i.-setting-up-the-local-integral-formulation">I. Setting Up the Local Integral Formulation</h2>
<p>Let <span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi mathvariant="double-struck">R</mi><mi>K</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q \in \mathbb{R}^K</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.73354em; vertical-align: -0.19444em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.03588em;">q</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.277778em;"></span><span class="mrel">∈</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.277778em;"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.841331em; vertical-align: 0em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathbb">R</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.841331em;"><span class="" style="top: -3.063em; margin-right: 0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mathnormal mtight" style="margin-right: 0.07153em;">K</span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span> be a query vector in latent space. Any nearby training point can be represented as <span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>z</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>q</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>u</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z = q + u</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.43056em; vertical-align: -0.19444em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.03588em;">q</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.222222em;"></span><span class="mbin">+</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.222222em;"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.43056em; vertical-align: 0em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal">u</span></span></span></span></span>, where <span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi mathvariant="double-struck">R</mi><mi>K</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u \in \mathbb{R}^K</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.5782em; vertical-align: 0em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathbb">R</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.841331em;"><span class="" style="top: -3.063em; margin-right: 0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mathnormal mtight" style="margin-right: 0.07153em;">K</span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span> is a small spatial displacement vector.</p>
<p>In the continuous asymptotic limit (as sample size <span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>→</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N \to \infty</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.68333em; vertical-align: 0em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.10903em;">N</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.277778em;"></span><span class="mrel">→</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.277778em;"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.43056em; vertical-align: 0em;"></span><span class="mord">∞</span></span></span></span></span> and bandwidth <span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>→</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h \to 0</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.69444em; vertical-align: 0em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal">h</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.277778em;"></span><span class="mrel">→</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.277778em;"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.64444em; vertical-align: 0em;"></span><span class="mord">0</span></span></span></span></span>), the Nadaraya-Watson kernel estimator computes the conditional expectation:</p>
<p><span class="katex--display"><span class="katex-display"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="block"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="double-struck">E</mi><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>y</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">]</mo><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><msub><mo>∫</mo><msup><mi mathvariant="double-struck">R</mi><mi>K</mi></msup></msub><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>u</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo> <mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>u</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo> <msub><mi>K</mi><mi>h</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>u</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo> <mi>d</mi><mi>u</mi></mrow><mrow><msub><mo>∫</mo><msup><mi mathvariant="double-struck">R</mi><mi>K</mi></msup></msub><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>u</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo> <msub><mi>K</mi><mi>h</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>u</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo> <mi>d</mi><mi>u</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{E}[\hat{y}(q)] = \frac{\int_{\mathbb{R}^K} y(q + u) \, p(q + u) \, K_h(u) \, du}{\int_{\mathbb{R}^K} p(q + u) \, K_h(u) \, du}</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 1em; <p>To evaluate this fraction, we expand the unknown non-linear target function <span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>u</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y(q + u)</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 1em; vertical-align: -0.25em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal">u</span><span class="mclose">)</span></span></span></span></span> and the unknown latent probability density <span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>u</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p(q + u)</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 1em; <h2 id="ii.-multivariate-2nd-order-taylor-series-expansions">II. Multivariate 2nd-Order Taylor Series Expansions</h2>
<p>Expanding the target function <span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>u</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y(q + u)</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 1em; vertical-align: -0.25em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.03588em;">y</span><span class="mopen">(</span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.03588em;">q</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.222222em;"></span><span class="mbin">+</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.222222em;"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 1em; vertical-align: -0.25em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal">u</span><span class="mclose">)</span></span></span></span></span> around <span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>q</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.625em; vertical-align: -0.19444em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.03588em;">q</span></span></span></span></span>:</p>
