<h2 id="v.-anatomy-of-the-bias-the-score-function-coupling">V. Anatomy of the Bias: The Score Function Coupling</h2>
<p>This derivation reveals that non-linear prediction error at <span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>q</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.625em; vertical-align: -0.19444em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.03588em;">q</span></span></span></span></span> consists of two distinct mathematical components:</p>
<ol>
<li><strong>Target Curvature (<span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta y(q)</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 1em; vertical-align: -0.25em;"></span><span class="mord">Δ</span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.03588em;">y</span><span class="mopen">(</span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.03588em;">q</span><span class="mclose">)</span></span></span></span></span>):</strong> The Laplacian of the task function. This represents the intrinsic non-linearity of the target boundary itself.</li>
<li><strong>Density-Gradient Coupling (<span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">∇</mi><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mi>T</mi></msup><mi mathvariant="normal">∇</mi><mi>log</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\nabla y(q)^T \nabla \log p(q)</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 1.09133em; vertical-align: -0.25em;"></span><span class="mord">∇</span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.03588em;">y</span><span class="mopen">(</span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.03588em;">q</span><span class="mclose"><span class="mclose">)</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.841331em;"><span class="" style="top: -3.063em; margin-right: 0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mathnormal mtight" style="margin-right: 0.13889em;">T</span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mord">∇</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.166667em;"></span><span class="mop">lo<span style="margin-right: 0.01389em;">g</span></span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.166667em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal">p</span><span class="mopen">(</span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.03588em;">q</span><span class="mclose">)</span></span></span></span></span>):</strong> The inner product between the task sensitivity vector <span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">∇</mi><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\nabla y(q)</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 1em; vertical-align: -0.25em;"></span><span class="mord">∇</span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.03588em;">y</span><span class="mopen">(</span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.03588em;">q</span><span class="mclose">)</span></span></span></span></span> and the <strong>Score Function</strong> of the latent space:</li>
</ol>
<p><span class="katex--display"><span class="katex-display"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="block"><semantics><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∇</mi><mi>log</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">∇</mi><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S(q) = \nabla \log p(q) = \frac{\nabla p(q)}{p(q)}</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 1em; vertical-align: -0.25em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.05764em;">S</span><span class="mopen">(</span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.03588em;">q</span><span class="mclose">)</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.277778em;"></span><span class="mrel">=</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.277778em;"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 1em; vertical-align: -0.25em;"></span><span class="mord">∇</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.166667em;"></span><span class="mop">lo<span style="margin-right: 0.01389em;">g</span></span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.166667em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal">p</span><span class="mopen">(</span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.03588em;">q</span><span class="mclose">)</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.277778em;"></span><span class="mrel">=</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.277778em;"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 2.363em; vertical-align: -0.936em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mopen nulldelimiter"></span><span class="mfrac"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 1.427em;"><span class="" style="top: -2.314em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 3em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal">p</span><span class="mopen">(</span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.03588em;">q</span><span class="mclose">)</span></span></span><span class="" style="top: -3.23em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 3em;"></span><span class="frac-line" style="border-bottom-width: 0.04em;"></span></span><span class="" style="top: -3.677em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 3em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord">∇</span><span class="mord mathnormal">p</span><span class="mopen">(</span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.03588em;">q</span><span class="mclose">)</span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.936em;"><span class=""></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mclose nulldelimiter"></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></p>
<h3 id="physical-meaning-of-the-coupling">Physical Meaning of the Coupling</h3>
<p>If the latent density <span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p(z)</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 1em; vertical-align: -0.25em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal">p</span><span class="mopen">(</span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.04398em;">z</span><span class="mclose">)</span></span></span></span></span> is non-uniform, its gradient <span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">∇</mi><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\nabla p(q)</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 1em; vertical-align: -0.25em;"></span><span class="mord">∇</span><span class="mord mathnormal">p</span><span class="mopen">(</span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.03588em;">q</span><span class="mclose">)</span></span></span></span></span> points toward the region of higher point concentration. When local samples are drawn to evaluate <span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>q</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.625em; vertical-align: -0.19444em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.03588em;">q</span></span></span></span></span>, they are disproportionately pulled toward higher-density regions.</p>
<p>If the downstream task changes value in that same direction (<span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">∇</mi><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo mathvariant="normal">≠</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\nabla y(q) \neq 0</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 1em; vertical-align: -0.25em;"></span><span class="mord">∇</span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.03588em;">y</span><span class="mopen">(</span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.03588em;">q</span><span class="mclose">)</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.277778em;"></span><span class="mrel"><span class="mrel"><span class="mord vbox"><span class="thinbox"><span class="rlap"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.88888em; vertical-align: -0.19444em;"></span><span class="inner"><span class="mord"><span class="mrel"></span></span></span><span class="fix"></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mrel">=</span></span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.277778em;"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.64444em; vertical-align: 0em;"></span><span class="mord">0</span></span></span></span></span>), this spatial asymmetry shifts the average prediction away from <span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y(q)</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 1em; vertical-align: -0.25em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.03588em;">y</span><span class="mopen">(</span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.03588em;">q</span><span class="mclose">)</span></span></span></span></span>.</p>
<p>The term <span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">∇</mi><mi>log</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\nabla \log p(q)</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 1em; vertical-align: -0.25em;"></span><span class="mord">∇</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.166667em;"></span><span class="mop">lo<span style="margin-right: 0.01389em;">g</span></span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.166667em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal">p</span><span class="mopen">(</span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.03588em;">q</span><span class="mclose">)</span></span></span></span></span> acts as a spatial force vector distorting non-linear predictions. In <strong>Response 3</strong>, we will integrate this pointwise squared bias over the entire latent manifold <span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi mathvariant="double-struck">R</mi><mi>K</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{R}^K</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.841331em; vertical-align: 0em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathbb">R</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.841331em;"><span class="" style="top: -3.063em; margin-right: 0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mathnormal mtight" style="margin-right: 0.07153em;">K</span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span> to reveal how the <strong>Fisher Information Functional <span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>J</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">J(p)</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 1em; vertical-align: -0.25em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.09618em;">J</span><span class="mopen">(</span><span class="mord mathnormal">p</span><span class="mclose">)</span></span></span></span></span></strong> naturally emerges.</p>
<h1 id="part-12-response-3-integrating-squared-bias--the-birth-of-jp">Part 12 (Response 3): Integrating Squared Bias &amp; The Birth of <span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>J</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">J(p)</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 1em; vertical-align: -0.25em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.09618em;">J</span><span class="mopen">(</span><span class="mord mathnormal">p</span><span class="mclose">)</span></span></span></span></span></h1>
<p>In Response 2, we derived the pointwise prediction bias at a specific query location <span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi mathvariant="double-struck">R</mi><mi>K</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q \in \mathbb{R}^K</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.73354em; vertical-align: -0.19444em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.03588em;">q</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.277778em;"></span><span class="mrel">∈</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.277778em;"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.841331em; vertical-align: 0em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathbb">R</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.841331em;"><span class="" style="top: -3.063em; margin-right: 0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mathnormal mtight" style="margin-right: 0.07153em;">K</span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span> for local non-linear estimators. To determine the global risk across the entire embedding space, we must integrate the squared pointwise bias over the full probability distribution <span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p(q)</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 1em; vertical-align: -0.25em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal">p</span><span class="mopen">(</span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.03588em;">q</span><span class="mclose">)</span></span></span></span></span> of the latent space.</p>
<hr>
<h2 id="i.-formulating-integrated-squared-bias-isb">I. Formulating Integrated Squared Bias (ISB)</h2>
<p>The global quality of a representation for a downstream task is measured by its <strong>Integrated Squared Bias (ISB)</strong>:</p>
<p><span class="katex--display"><span class="katex-display"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="block"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ISB</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mo>:</mo><mo>=</mo><msub><mo>∫</mo><msup><mi mathvariant="double-struck">R</mi><mi>K</mi></msup></msub><msup><mrow><mo fence="true">(</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Bias</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>y</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo fence="true">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo> <mi>d</mi><mi>q</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\operatorname{ISB} := \int_{\mathbb{R}^K} \left( \operatorname{Bias}(\hat{y}(q)) \right)^2 p(q) \, dq</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.68333em; vertical-align: 0em;"></span><span class="mop"><span class="mord mathrm">ISB</span></span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.277778em;"></span><span class="mrel">:=</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.277778em;"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 2.27195em; <h3 id="bounding-downstream-task-regularity">Bounding Downstream Task Regularity</h3>
<p>During self-supervised pre-training, the downstream task is unknown. However, we assume any valid downstream task possesses smooth, bounded physical properties:</p>
<ol>
<li><strong>Bounded Target Curvature:</strong> The target Laplacian is strictly bounded by a constant <span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>B</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.68333em; vertical-align: 0em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.05017em;">B</span></span></span></span></span>, such that <span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">∣</mi><mrow></mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∣</mi><mrow></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mi>B</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\vert{}\Delta y(q)\vert{} \le B</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 1em; vertical-align: -0.25em;"></span><span class="mord">∣</span><span class="mord"></span><span class="mord">Δ</span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.03588em;">y</span><span class="mopen">(</span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.03588em;">q</span><span class="mclose">)</span><span class="mord">∣</span><span class="mord"></span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.277778em;"></span><span class="mrel">≤</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.277778em;"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.68333em; vertical-align: 0em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.05017em;">B</span></span></span></span></span>.</li>
<li><strong>Bounded Target Gradient:</strong> The target task gradient (sensitivity) is bounded by a Lipschitz constant <span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>L</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.68333em; vertical-align: 0em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal">L</span></span></span></span></span>, such that <span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">∥</mi><mrow></mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">∇</mi><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∥</mi><mrow></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mi>L</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Vert{}\nabla y(q)\Vert{} \le L</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 1em; vertical-align: -0.25em;"></span><span class="mord">∥</span><span class="mord"></span><span class="mord">∇</span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.03588em;">y</span><span class="mopen">(</span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.03588em;">q</span><span class="mclose">)</span><span class="mord">∥</span><span class="mord"></span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.277778em;"></span><span class="mrel">≤</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.277778em;"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.68333em; vertical-align: 0em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal">L</span></span></span></span></span>.</li>
</ol>
<p>Factoring these worst-case bounds out of the integrals:</p>
<p><span class="katex--display"><span class="katex-display"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="block"><semantics><mrow><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ISB</mi><mo>⁡</mo></mrow><mtext>kernel</mtext></msub><mo>≤</mo><msup><mrow><mo fence="true">(</mo><mfrac><mrow><msup><mi>h</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><msub><mi>μ</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>K</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo fence="true">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mrow><mo fence="true">[</mo><mn>2</mn><msup><mi>B</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><msub><mo>∫</mo><msup><mi mathvariant="double-struck">R</mi><mi>K</mi></msup></msub><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo> <mi>d</mi><mi>q</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>8</mn><msup><mi>L</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><msub><mo>∫</mo><msup><mi mathvariant="double-struck">R</mi><mi>K</mi></msup></msub><mi mathvariant="normal">∥</mi><mrow></mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">∇</mi><mi>log</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∥</mi><msup><mrow></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo> <mi>d</mi><mi>q</mi><mo fence="true">]</mo></mrow><mo>+</mo><mi>o</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>h</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\operatorname{ISB}_{\text{kernel}} \le \left( \frac{h^2 \mu_2(K)}{2} \right)^2 \left[ 2 B^2 \int_{\mathbb{R}^K} p(q) \, dq + 8 L^2 \int_{\mathbb{R}^K} \Vert{}\nabla \log p(q)\Vert{}^2 p(q) \, dq \right] + o(h^4)</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.83333em; <p><span class="katex--display"><span class="katex-display"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="block"><semantics><mrow><mi>I</mi><mi>S</mi><msub><mi>B</mi><mtext>kernel</mtext></msub><mo>≤</mo><msup><mrow><mo fence="true">(</mo><mfrac><mrow><msup><mi>h</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><msub><mi>μ</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>K</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo fence="true">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mrow><mo fence="true">(</mo><mn>2</mn><msup><mi>B</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>8</mn><msup><mi>L</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mi>J</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo fence="true">)</mo></mrow><mo>+</mo><mi>o</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>h</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">ISB_{\text{kernel}} \le \left( \frac{h^2 \mu_2(K)}{2} \right)^2 \left( 2B^2 + 8L^2 J(p) \right) + o(h^4)</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.83333em; <p>This provides the core proof of Part 12: To minimize worst-case estimation risk across all possible non-linear downstream tasks, a Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture must construct an embedding density <span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p(z)</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 1em; vertical-align: -0.25em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal">p</span><span class="mopen">(</span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.04398em;">z</span><span class="mclose">)</span></span></span></span></span> that minimizes the Fisher Information Functional <span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>J</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">J(p)</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 1em; vertical-align: -0.25em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.09618em;">J</span><span class="mopen">(</span><span class="mord mathnormal">p</span><span class="mclose">)</span></span></span></span></span> under a fixed scale constraint.</p>

<p>In <strong>Response 4</strong>, we will strip away the calculus and analyze the physical and geometric meaning of <span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>J</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">J(p)</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 1em; <h1 id="part-12-response-4-geometric--physical-intuition-of-the-fisher-information-bottleneck">Part 12 (Response 4): Geometric &amp; Physical Intuition of the Fisher Information Bottleneck</h1>

<p>To understand why this equation dictates modern self-supervised JEPA design, we must strip away the calculus and inspect what <span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>J</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">J(p)</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 1em; vertical-align: -0.25em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.09618em;">J</span><span class="mopen">(</span><span class="mord mathnormal">p</span><span class="mclose">)</span></span></span></span></span> measures physically and geometrically inside the high-dimensional latent manifold.</p>
<hr>
<h2 id="i.-what-does-jp-measure-physically">I. What Does <span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>J</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">J(p)</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 1em; vertical-align: -0.25em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.09618em;">J</span><span class="mopen">(</span><span class="mord mathnormal">p</span><span class="mclose">)</span></span></span></span></span> Measure Physically?</h2>
<p>In probability theory, the <strong>Score Function</strong> of a density <span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p(x)</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 1em; vertical-align: -0.25em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal">p</span><span class="mopen">(</span><span class="mord mathnormal">x</span><span class="mclose">)</span></span></span></span></span> is defined as the gradient of its log-density:</p>
<p><span class="katex--display"><span class="katex-display"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="block"><semantics><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>:</mo><mo>=</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∇</mi><mi>log</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">∇</mi><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S(x) := \nabla \log p(x) = \frac{\nabla p(x)}{p(x)}</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 1em; vertical-align: -0.25em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.05764em;">S</span><span class="mopen">(</span><span class="mord mathnormal">x</span><span class="mclose">)</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.277778em;"></span><span class="mrel">:=</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.277778em;"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 1em; vertical-align: -0.25em;"></span><span class="mord">∇</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.166667em;"></span><span class="mop">lo<span style="margin-right: 0.01389em;">g</span></span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.166667em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal">p</span><span class="mopen">(</span><span class="mord mathnormal">x</span><span class="mclose">)</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.277778em;"></span><span class="mrel">=</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.277778em;"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 2.363em; vertical-align: -0.936em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mopen nulldelimiter"></span><span class="mfrac"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 1.427em;"><span class="" style="top: -2.314em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 3em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal">p</span><span class="mopen">(</span><span class="mord mathnormal">x</span><span class="mclose">)</span></span></span><span class="" style="top: -3.23em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 3em;"></span><span class="frac-line" style="border-bottom-width: 0.04em;"></span></span><span class="" style="top: -3.677em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 3em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord">∇</span><span class="mord mathnormal">p</span><span class="mopen">(</span><span class="mord mathnormal">x</span><span class="mclose">)</span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.936em;"><span class=""></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mclose nulldelimiter"></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></p>
<p>Geometrically, the score vector <span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S(x)</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 1em; vertical-align: -0.25em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.05764em;">S</span><span class="mopen">(</span><span class="mord mathnormal">x</span><span class="mclose">)</span></span></span></span></span> acts as an attractive force vector at point <span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.43056em; vertical-align: 0em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal">x</span></span></span></span></span>. It points in the direction of steepest density increase, with a magnitude proportional to how rapidly the relative point concentration changes.</p>
<p>The Fisher Information Functional <span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>J</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">J(p)</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 1em; vertical-align: -0.25em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.09618em;">J</span><span class="mopen">(</span><span class="mord mathnormal">p</span><span class="mclose">)</span></span></span></span></span> is simply the <strong>expected squared magnitude (energy) of this score vector</strong> across the entire distribution:</p>
<p><span class="katex--display"><span class="katex-display"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="block"><semantics><mrow><mi>J</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="double-struck">E</mi><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>∼</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow></msub><mrow><mo fence="true">[</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∥</mi><mrow></mrow><mi>S</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∥</mi><msup><mrow></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo fence="true">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">J(p) = \mathbb{E}_{x \sim p}\left[ \Vert{}S(x)\Vert{}^2 \right]</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 1em; vertical-align: -0.25em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.09618em;">J</span><span class="mopen">(</span><span class="mord mathnormal">p</span><span class="mclose">)</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.277778em;"></span><span class="mrel">=</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.277778em;"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 1.21412em; vertical-align: -0.35001em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathbb">E</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.151392em;"><span class="" style="top: -2.55em; margin-left: 0em; margin-right: 0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight"><span class="mord mathnormal mtight">x</span><span class="mrel mtight">∼</span><span class="mord mathnormal mtight">p</span></span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.286108em;"><span class=""></span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.166667em;"></span><span class="minner"><span class="mopen delimcenter" style="top: 0em;"><span class="delimsizing size1">[</span></span><span class="mord">∥</span><span class="mord"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.05764em;">S</span><span class="mopen">(</span><span class="mord mathnormal">x</span><span class="mclose">)</span><span class="mord">∥</span><span class="mord"><span class="mord"></span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.864108em;"><span class="" style="top: -3.113em; margin-right: 0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight">2</span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mclose delimcenter" style="top: 0em;"><span class="delimsizing size1">]</span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></p>
<h3 id="the-physical-analogy-manifold-surface-tension--topological-wrinkling">The Physical Analogy: “Manifold Surface Tension” / “Topological Wrinkling”</h3>
<p>Think of the latent probability density <span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p(x)</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 1em; vertical-align: -0.25em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal">p</span><span class="mopen">(</span><span class="mord mathnormal">x</span><span class="mclose">)</span></span></span></span></span> as a physical fluid spread across <span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi mathvariant="double-struck">R</mi><mi>K</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{R}^K</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.841331em; vertical-align: 0em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathbb">R</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.841331em;"><span class="" style="top: -3.063em; margin-right: 0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mathnormal mtight" style="margin-right: 0.07153em;">K</span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span>:</p>
<ul>
<li><strong>High <span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>J</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">J(p)</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 1em; vertical-align: -0.25em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.09618em;">J</span><span class="mopen">(</span><span class="mord mathnormal">p</span><span class="mclose">)</span></span></span></span></span></strong> corresponds to a <strong>highly wrinkled, turbulent fluid surface</strong>. The density fluctuates wildly over short spatial distances.</li>
<li><strong>Low <span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>J</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">J(p)</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 1em; vertical-align: -0.25em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.09618em;">J</span><span class="mopen">(</span><span class="mord mathnormal">p</span><span class="mclose">)</span></span></span></span></span></strong> corresponds to a <strong>smooth, gently sloped, dispersed fluid surface</strong> with minimal local variation.</li>
</ul>
<p>Thus, <span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>J</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">J(p)</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 1em; vertical-align: -0.25em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.09618em;">J</span><span class="mopen">(</span><span class="mord mathnormal">p</span><span class="mclose">)</span></span></span></span></span> acts as a direct measure of <strong>latent space roughness</strong>.</p>
<hr>
<h2 id="ii.-high-jp-vs.-low-jp-latent-geometries">II. High <span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>J</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">J(p)</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 1em; vertical-align: -0.25em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.09618em;">J</span><span class="mopen">(</span><span class="mord mathnormal">p</span><span class="mclose">)</span></span></span></span></span> vs. Low <span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>J</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">J(p)</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 1em; vertical-align: -0.25em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.09618em;">J</span><span class="mopen">(</span><span class="mord mathnormal">p</span><span class="mclose">)</span></span></span></span></span> Latent Geometries</h2>
<p>To see why <span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>J</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">J(p)</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 1em; vertical-align: -0.25em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.09618em;">J</span><span class="mopen">(</span><span class="mord mathnormal">p</span><span class="mclose">)</span></span></span></span></span> corrupts non-linear estimation, let’s contrast two embedding spaces that contain the exact same data points, but organize their probability distributions differently:</p>
<pre><code>HIGH J(p): Wrinkled &amp; Spiky                 LOW J(p): Smooth &amp; Isotropic
       ▲                                          ▲
  ▲    │   ▲                                 ┌────┴────┐
  │    │   │                                /           \
──┴────┴───┴──────► z                      ─┴─────────────┴─► z
(High local gradients)                     (Gentle, uniform spread)

</code></pre>
<h3 id="the-high-jp-geometry-sharp-spikes--narrow-clusters">1. The High <span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>J</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">J(p)</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 1em; vertical-align: -0.25em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.09618em;">J</span><span class="mopen">(</span><span class="mord mathnormal">p</span><span class="mclose">)</span></span></span></span></span> Geometry (Sharp Spikes &amp; Narrow Clusters)</h3>
<p>Consider an embedding space where the encoder clusters images into tightly compressed, isolated islands separated by large empty voids.</p>
<ul>
<li>
<p><strong>Mathematical Condition:</strong> Near the edge of a cluster, the density <span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p(x)</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 1em; vertical-align: -0.25em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal">p</span><span class="mopen">(</span><span class="mord mathnormal">x</span><span class="mclose">)</span></span></span></span></span> drops rapidly toward zero, making the spatial gradient <span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">∇</mi><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\nabla p(x)</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 1em; vertical-align: -0.25em;"></span><span class="mord">∇</span><span class="mord mathnormal">p</span><span class="mopen">(</span><span class="mord mathnormal">x</span><span class="mclose">)</span></span></span></span></span> very steep.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><strong>The Explosion in <span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>J</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">J(p)</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 1em; vertical-align: -0.25em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.09618em;">J</span><span class="mopen">(</span><span class="mord mathnormal">p</span><span class="mclose">)</span></span></span></span></span>:</strong> Because <span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p(x)</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 1em; vertical-align: -0.25em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal">p</span><span class="mopen">(</span><span class="mord mathnormal">x</span><span class="mclose">)</span></span></span></span></span> is in the denominator of <span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">∥</mi><mrow></mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">∇</mi><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∥</mi><msup><mrow></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{\Vert{}\nabla p(x)\Vert{}^2}{p(x)}</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 1.62892em; vertical-align: -0.52em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mopen nulldelimiter"></span><span class="mfrac"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 1.10892em;"><span class="" style="top: -2.655em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 3em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight"><span class="mord mathnormal mtight">p</span><span class="mopen mtight">(</span><span class="mord mathnormal mtight">x</span><span class="mclose mtight">)</span></span></span></span><span class="" style="top: -3.23em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 3em;"></span><span class="frac-line" style="border-bottom-width: 0.04em;"></span></span><span class="" style="top: -3.485em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 3em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight"><span class="mord mtight">∥</span><span class="mord mtight"></span><span class="mord mtight">∇</span><span class="mord mathnormal mtight">p</span><span class="mopen mtight">(</span><span class="mord mathnormal mtight">x</span><span class="mclose mtight">)</span><span class="mord mtight">∥</span><span class="mord mtight"><span class="mord mtight"></span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.891314em;"><span class="" style="top: -2.931em; margin-right: 0.0714286em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 2.5em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size3 size1 mtight"><span class="mord mtight">2</span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.52em;"><span class=""></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mclose nulldelimiter"></span></span></span></span></span></span>, a region where density is low but changing rapidly causes <span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>J</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">J(p)</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 1em; vertical-align: -0.25em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.09618em;">J</span><span class="mopen">(</span><span class="mord mathnormal">p</span><span class="mclose">)</span></span></span></span></span> to explode.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><strong>The Failure Mechanism for Non-Linear Probes:</strong> Suppose a query point <span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>q</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.625em; vertical-align: -0.19444em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.03588em;">q</span></span></span></span></span> lies slightly off the center of a tight cluster. When <span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.69444em; vertical-align: 0em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.03148em;">k</span></span></span></span></span>-NN or kernel regression samples neighbors within a radius <span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>r</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_0</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.58056em; vertical-align: -0.15em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.02778em;">r</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.301108em;"><span class="" style="top: -2.55em; margin-left: -0.02778em; margin-right: 0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight">0</span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.15em;"><span class=""></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span> around <span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>q</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.625em; vertical-align: -0.19444em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.03588em;">q</span></span></span></span></span>, the asymmetric density force <span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">∇</mi><mi>log</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\nabla \log p(q)</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 1em; vertical-align: -0.25em;"></span><span class="mord">∇</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.166667em;"></span><span class="mop">lo<span style="margin-right: 0.01389em;">g</span></span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.166667em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal">p</span><span class="mopen">(</span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.03588em;">q</span><span class="mclose">)</span></span></span></span></span> violently pulls the “center of mass” of those samples toward the dense core. The local estimator predicts the target value of the cluster core rather than the true target at <span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>q</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.625em; vertical-align: -0.19444em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.03588em;">q</span></span></span></span></span>, introducing massive <strong>pointwise bias</strong>.</p>
</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="the-low-jp-geometry-smooth--uniform-manifold">2. The Low <span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>J</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">J(p)</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 1em; vertical-align: -0.25em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.09618em;">J</span><span class="mopen">(</span><span class="mord mathnormal">p</span><span class="mclose">)</span></span></span></span></span> Geometry (Smooth &amp; Uniform Manifold)</h3>
<p>Now consider an embedding space where points are distributed smoothly and continuously across the latent manifold without isolated spikes or artificial voids.</p>
<ul>
<li>
<p><strong>Mathematical Condition:</strong> Density gradients <span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">∇</mi><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\nabla p(x)</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 1em; vertical-align: -0.25em;"></span><span class="mord">∇</span><span class="mord mathnormal">p</span><span class="mopen">(</span><span class="mord mathnormal">x</span><span class="mclose">)</span></span></span></span></span> are small and vary gradually relative to the local density <span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p(x)</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 1em; vertical-align: -0.25em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal">p</span><span class="mopen">(</span><span class="mord mathnormal">x</span><span class="mclose">)</span></span></span></span></span>.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><strong>The Minimization of <span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>J</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">J(p)</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 1em; vertical-align: -0.25em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.09618em;">J</span><span class="mopen">(</span><span class="mord mathnormal">p</span><span class="mclose">)</span></span></span></span></span>:</strong> The score vectors <span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S(x)</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 1em; vertical-align: -0.25em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.05764em;">S</span><span class="mopen">(</span><span class="mord mathnormal">x</span><span class="mclose">)</span></span></span></span></span> have small magnitudes everywhere, driving <span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>J</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">J(p)</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 1em; vertical-align: -0.25em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.09618em;">J</span><span class="mopen">(</span><span class="mord mathnormal">p</span><span class="mclose">)</span></span></span></span></span> toward its mathematical floor.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><strong>The Success Mechanism for Non-Linear Probes:</strong> For any query point <span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>q</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.625em; vertical-align: -0.19444em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.03588em;">q</span></span></span></span></span>, neighboring training samples within radius <span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>r</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_0</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.58056em; vertical-align: -0.15em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.02778em;">r</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.301108em;"><span class="" style="top: -2.55em; margin-left: -0.02778em; margin-right: 0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight">0</span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 0.15em;"><span class=""></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span> are distributed nearly symmetrically around <span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>q</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.625em; vertical-align: -0.19444em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.03588em;">q</span></span></span></span></span>. The local density force <span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">∇</mi><mi>log</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>≈</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\nabla \log p(q) \approx 0</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 1em; vertical-align: -0.25em;"></span><span class="mord">∇</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.166667em;"></span><span class="mop">lo<span style="margin-right: 0.01389em;">g</span></span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.166667em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal">p</span><span class="mopen">(</span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.03588em;">q</span><span class="mclose">)</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.277778em;"></span><span class="mrel">≈</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.277778em;"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.64444em; vertical-align: 0em;"></span><span class="mord">0</span></span></span></span></span>, so the sample average converges smoothly to the true function value <span class="katex--inline"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y(q)</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 1em; vertical-align: -0.25em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.03588em;">y</span><span class="mopen">(</span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.03588em;">q</span><span class="mclose">)</span></span></span></span></span> without directional skew.</p>
</li>
</ul>
<hr>
<h2 id="iii.-the-fisher-bottleneck-paradox-why-variance-loss-alone-fails">III. The Fisher Bottleneck Paradox: Why Variance Loss Alone Fails</h2>
<p>This physical intuition exposes the fatal blind spot of early self-supervised loss functions (like pure VICReg):</p>
<p><span class="katex--display"><span class="katex-display"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="block"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="script">L</mi><mtext>variance</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>d</mi></mfrac><munderover><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>d</mi></munderover><mi>max</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo separator="true">,</mo><mi>γ</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>S</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>z</mi><mi>j</mi></msup><mo separator="true">,</mo><mi>ϵ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}_{\text{variance}} = \frac{1}{d} \sum_{j=1}^d \max(0, \gamma - S(z^j, \epsilon))</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 0.83333em; margin-left: 0em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 3.05em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight"><span class="mord mathnormal mtight" style="margin-right: 0.05724em;">j</span><span class="mrel mtight">=</span><span class="mord mtight">1</span></span></span></span><span class="" style="top: -3.05001em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 3.05em;"></span><span class=""><span class="mop op-symbol large-op">∑</span></span></span><span class="" style="top: -4.30001em; margin-left: 0em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height: 3.05em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mathnormal mtight">d</span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height: 1.41378em;"><span class=""></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.166667em;"></span><span class="mop">max</span><span class="mopen">(</span><span class="mord">0</span><span class="mpunct">,</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.166667em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right: 0.05556em;">γ</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.222222em;"></span><span class="mbin">−</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right: 0.222222em;"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height: 1.12466em;
